artigo.texto: BYD Files Immersion-Cooling Patent as JPMorgan Cuts Rating and September Volumes Roll In Published on 10/06/2026 at 12:11 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has lodged a patent application for a battery-cooling concept that submerges cell modules entirely in a dielectric fluid, adding a fresh layer to the Chinese automaker's technology pipeline even as its shares labour under a double-digit year-to-date decline. China's intellectual property authority published the filing yesterday, according to media reports. The original submission dates back to March 2025. Rather than routing coolant through channels along the outer faces of the modules, the described method lets a non-conductive liquid circulate directly around individual storage cells — an approach known as immersion cooling. That direct contact yields more uniform heat dissipation and can smooth out temperature spikes during operation. Thermal behaviour ranks as a decisive factor for the efficiency, durability and safety of high-voltage batteries, particularly under heavy charging loads or demanding use. September Output and Deliveries in Focus On the operational front, BYD reported production of 463,864 new-energy vehicles for September alongside sales of 463,561 units, figures the company flagged as preliminary and unaudited. Battery-electric passenger cars accounted for the bulk of deliveries at 273,143 units, while plug-in hybrids contributed 183,570 vehicles. Exports of new-energy vehicles reached 180,700 units during the month, underscoring the growing weight of overseas business. The broader picture is less buoyant. Across the first nine months of the calendar year, cumulative sales totalled 3,131,576 vehicles — a decline of 3.94 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. In German trading, the stock closed Monday at EUR 8.53, a daily gain of 1.6 percent. Since the start of the year, however, the shares have shed 20 percent. At a current price of EUR 8.52, the paper sits 6.1 percent above its 52-week low. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Model Offensive Meets a Regulatory Hurdle BYD is pressing ahead with an expansion of its line-up to reignite demand. Deliveries of the Formula S for the Fang Cheng Bao sub-brand began in late September, priced in China between 189,900 and 229,900 yuan. Management expects monthly sales of more than 10,000 to as many as 15,000 units over the medium term when the GT variant is included. Customer registration has also opened for the Ti 9, with first deliveries of the SUV flagship slated for the fourth quarter. A symbolic milestone arrived on the production line: on 29 September, the Da Han flagship sedan became the ten-millionth vehicle to roll off the Dynasty series. The official market launch of the new model is set for 13 October. Not everything went smoothly. China's market regulator announced a recall on 18 September covering 183,211 vehicles from the Tang and Qin model lines, citing potentially defective brake-pedal bump stops that the manufacturer will replace free of charge. JPMorgan Steps to the Sidelines Analysts at JPMorgan downgraded the stock from Overweight to Neutral on 29 September, trimming the price target to HKD 88 from HKD 124. The brokerage pointed to anticipated weakness in China's auto sector in the second half of 2026, subdued domestic demand and rising input costs. It also flagged political uncertainties and tariff as well as non-tariff trade barriers facing BYD's global expansion. Shareholders, meanwhile, signed off on governance matters at the most recent annual general meeting, approving charter amendments, board elections, director remuneration and an asset-pool transaction involving external guarantees. With the share price trading below its long-term moving averages, the market is showing restraint about the company's continued expansion and margin trajectory at home. artigo.texto: O governo federal ampliou a relação de máquinas e equipamentos que poderão ser importados com redução do Imposto de Importação, incluindo tecnologias de inteligência artificial, processamento de dados, criptografia, telecomunicações, automação industrial e equipamentos para o setor elétrico. As mudanças constam das Resoluções Gecex nº 970, 971 e 973, de 6 de outubro, publicadas nesta quarta-feira (7) no Diário Oficial da União. Para entender o alcance das medidas é preciso explicar o que é um Ex-tarifário. Em vez de reduzir o imposto de todos os produtos enquadrados em determinada categoria aduaneira, o governo cria uma exceção, o “Ex”, para uma máquina ou equipamento com características técnicas muito específicas. Quando atendidos os requisitos do regime, especialmente a inexistência de produção nacional equivalente nos termos das regras aplicáveis, a alíquota de importação pode ser reduzida temporariamente. Isso significa que a decisão não beneficia, por exemplo, qualquer computador, roteador ou equipamento de inteligência artificial importado. O produto precisa corresponder à descrição técnica estabelecida pelo governo para aquele Ex-tarifário. As medidas publicadas agora não alteram o Redata, regime criado para estimular investimentos em data centers. Elas fazem uma atualização das listas de Ex-tarifários de Bens de Capital (BK), que abrangem máquinas e equipamentos utilizados na produção, e de Bens de Informática e Telecomunicações (BIT). Inteligência artificial Uma das novidades da Resolução Gecex nº 971 está na NCM 8471.50.10. O governo criou o Ex 044 para unidades de processamento automático de dados destinadas a aplicações de inteligência artificial, análise de vídeo e telemetria veicular. Em termos mais simples, trata-se de um computador especializado instalado em veículos. Ele recebe imagens de câmeras e informações de sensores, processa esses dados no próprio equipamento e consegue identificar situações de risco. A descrição publicada pelo Gecex prevê, por exemplo, análise de vídeo em tempo real para detectar fadiga do motorista, uso de telefone celular, tabagismo, distração e ausência do cinto de segurança. O equipamento pode então produzir alertas sonoros e visuais. Não se trata, portanto, de um servidor genérico de inteligência artificial ou de uma GPU para data center. É um sistema dedicado principalmente ao processamento de imagens e informações dentro de veículos. O benefício tem vigência prevista até 30 de setembro de 2028. Criptomoedas A resolução também concede Ex-tarifário para uma máquina cuja finalidade é bastante específica: mineração de criptomoedas. O Ex 033 da NCM 8471.50.90 abrange equipamentos eletrônicos destinados ao processamento criptográfico baseado no algoritmo Equihash. Na prática, são computadores construídos especialmente para executar, repetidamente e em grande velocidade, os cálculos matemáticos utilizados para validar operações e gerar novas unidades de determinadas criptomoedas. A máquina descrita pelo governo utiliza múltiplos processadores especializados do tipo ASIC, sigla em inglês para circuito integrado desenvolvido para uma aplicação específica. Diferentemente de um computador comum, que pode executar inúmeras tarefas, um ASIC é projetado para fazer determinada operação com grande eficiência. O equipamento beneficiado precisa alcançar capacidade de processamento de 840 kSol/s, ter consumo máximo de 3.200 watts, refrigeração por ventilação forçada e conexão Ethernet. O Equihash é utilizado por criptomoedas como a Zcash. Portanto, o Ex não representa genericamente uma desoneração de qualquer equipamento destinado à mineração de criptomoedas. Criptografia Outro item incluído na relação ajuda a mostrar que a resolução alcança tecnologias que normalmente permanecem invisíveis para o usuário. O governo concedeu Ex para módulos de segurança criptográfica conhecidos como TPM, Trusted Platform Module. Um TPM funciona como uma espécie de cofre eletrônico dentro de um computador ou equipamento digital. Em vez de deixar determinadas chaves criptográficas e credenciais protegidas apenas por software, o dispositivo mantém essas informações em um componente físico dedicado. Ele pode ser utilizado para armazenar chaves de criptografia, verificar se um equipamento foi adulterado e comprovar que o sistema iniciou utilizando componentes considerados confiáveis. É uma tecnologia encontrada em computadores e também utilizada em equipamentos corporativos e sistemas que exigem níveis mais elevados de segurança.

artigo.texto: Inlyte Energy, a United States-based iron-sodium battery storage manufacturer, has announced a long-duration storage project with CutPeak Energy at Berkshire East Mountain Resort in Massachusetts. The project has been designed around the resort's energy profile, since its snowmaking pushes the electricity demand as high as 4 MW for a small part of the year. An iron-sodium battery of up to 80 MWh is therefore to be recharged during the long hours of low demand and to deliver power through the snowmaking peaks. During a grid outage, the same battery can be switched to the critical loads which keep the resort open as a shelter and a warming centre. The project is one of two demonstrations that the state has selected under its $40.3 million Advancing Massachusetts Power Energy Storage Grant Program. Under that award, the battery is to come online in 2028, and the project remains subject to final agreements, financing and approvals. artigo.texto: A BYD já definiu como pretende organizar suas marcas de luxo no Brasil. Em conversa com executivos da empresa durante o evento de apresentação da Denza, em Campos do Jordão (SP), o grupo confirmou, nesta terça-feira (6), que a Yangwang será sua marca topo de linha no País, posicionada acima da própria Denza. A estratégia terá, portanto, três níveis. A BYD continuará como marca principal do grupo, enquanto a Denza ocupará o espaço de premium de luxo e a Yangwang ficará no degrau mais alto, com a missão de disputar espaço com fabricantes de altíssimo luxo e desempenho. Segundo os executivos, a Yangwang terá como referências marcas como McLaren, Rolls-Royce e Aston Martin, além de fabricantes que também estudam avançar nesse segmento no Brasil, como a Cadillac. Durante a conversa, Marcelo Albino, Head de Produtos Denza e Desenvolvimento de Negócios na BYD Auto Brasil, classificou a Yangwang como aquilo que há de melhor atualmente em termos de automóveis produzidos na China. E já há um evento oficial de apresentação da nova divisão, que ocorrerá em Dubai (Emirados Árabes Unidos), no início de novembro. U7, U8 e U9 estão no radar A BYD ainda não definiu uma data para a chegada dos primeiros modelos da Yangwang ao mercado brasileiro. Existe, porém, um estudo de mercado em andamento e a expectativa é de que U7, U8 e U9 estejam entre os produtos avaliados para o País. Os três modelos representam diferentes propostas dentro da Yangwang. Resumidamente, o U7 é um sedã de luxo 100% elétrico; U8 será o SUV que atravessa alagamentos e rios; e o U9 é o cupê esportivo que atinge 490 km/h. A marca tem justamente a estratégia de atuar no segmento mais sofisticado do mercado, combinando alto desempenho, tecnologia e acabamento de extremo luxo, acima, por incrível que parece, de modelos como Porsche Panamera ou Taycan. Os executivos, no entanto, evitaram estabelecer um cronograma para a chegada dos carros. Portanto, a vinda dos modelos é tratada neste momento como uma possibilidade em estudo, e não como lançamento confirmado. Essa previsão só deve acontecer no evento de Dubai. Primeira loja deve ser em São Paulo Segundo Werner Schaal, Diretor Comercial da Denza Brasil, há interesse em expandir a rede tanto da Yangwang quanto da Denza. A expectativa é que a primeira concessionária da Yangwang no Brasil seja instalada em São Paulo, mas a BYD ainda não fechou todos os detalhes da operação. A intenção é ampliar posteriormente a presença da marca para outras regiões do País. Deve ser uma rede menor que a da Denza, portanto, não haverá uma replicação ou carros da Yangwang dentro de lojas da Denza, por exemplo. A tendência é que as duas marcas tenham concessionárias independentes, sem necessariamente dividir o mesmo endereço ou a mesma operação física. Apesar disso, o time que atualmente cuida da Denza dentro da estrutura da BYD também deverá assumir a operação da Yangwang no Brasil. Segundo os interlocutores ouvidos pelo Jornal do Carro, A estratégia indica que a BYD não pretende tratar suas marcas premium apenas como versões mais caras de seus carros convencionais. A ideia é criar uma estrutura própria para cada uma delas, com posicionamento e público diferentes. LEIA MAIS: - Aceleramos o YangWang U8, SUV da nova marca BYD no Brasil - BYD em Pequim: esportivo elétrico, SUVs de luxo e carro conceito que vira cinema - Após cancelamento, CFMoto anuncia nova data de lote de 700 motos Os executivos também destacaram a velocidade de evolução da indústria automobilística chinesa. A avaliação da BYD é que a transformação tecnológica do setor continuará acontecendo rapidamente e que fabricantes que demorarem a acompanhar esse movimento já estarão em desvantagem. A chegada da Yangwang representa justamente o passo seguinte dessa estratégia: depois de avançar sobre segmentos de volume com a BYD e entrar no mercado premium com a Denza, o grupo quer disputar também o espaço reservado às marcas de maior prestígio e preço. Ainda não há, desta forma, uma data definida para a estreia da Yangwang no Brasil. Mas a confirmação de que a marca será posicionada no topo da estrutura da BYD coloca o País no radar para receber alguns dos modelos mais sofisticados desenvolvidos pelo grupo chinês. artigo.texto: KINGSTON, N.Y. — The city’s Common Council unanimously approved creating a task force to draft zoning regulations for utility-scale battery energy storage systems after proposals for such facilities caused controversy in neighboring communities. The Common Council approved the creation of the task force at its meeting on Tuesday, Oct. 6. After the proposal was modified by increasing the task force’s size to nine members, it was approved by an 8-0 vote. Teryl Mickens, D-Ward 5, was absent. Majority Leader Michele Hirsch said the city will commit to “full accountability,” with all task force meetings “strictly complying” with the state’s open meetings law. Hirsch said the task force will have a clearly defined six-month timeframe to do “comprehensive research,” collaborate with “stakeholders” and external experts on battery energy storage systems and draft new zoning regulations. This will allow the city to get ahead of any major project proposals with “thoughtful, legally sound zoning codes,” according to Hirsch. However, lawmakers have stated they are not certain if a lithium-ion battery energy storage facility could even be located in the city. When asked by a reporter in an email after September’s Laws and Rules Committee meeting, Common Council President Andrea Shaut said she does not believe there are any locations in the city where such a facility could be located. Such facilities consist of lithium-iron-phosphate battery cells packaged into modules, about the size of oversized briefcases, which are then put into racks and stored in containers resembling shipping containers. The facilities require proximity to a utility’s substation. The five proposals in Ulster County — three in the town of Ulster, one in Saugerties and one in New Paltz — are all proposed near a Central Hudson substation. Proposed lithium-ion battery energy storage projects, including the three projects proposed in the neighboring town of Ulster, have met with controversy across the county. Two of those projects, on Hurley Avenue in the town of Ulster, are close to the city line. Mission Clean Energy has proposed a 120-megawatt lithium-ion battery facility on a 7.3-acre site at 463-465 Hurley Ave. That project is about 500 feet west of the controversial Terra-Gen site at the former John A. Coleman Catholic High School, where the Town Board is being asked to approve a 250-megawatt lithium-ion facility on 15 acres. In the town of Ulster, board members are also reviewing a proposal from BayWa r.e. for a 150-megawatt lithium-ion battery facility on Frank Sottile Boulevard. It would be on about 10.4 acres adjacent to the former town landfill, with a new substation constructed on the other side of the road. It would be adjacent to a residential neighborhood and the 164-unit Ulster Gardens apartment complex. In the town of Saugerties, Key Capture Energy has proposed a 100-megawatt facility on Tomson’s Road near a Central Hudson substation that has met with opposition from residents and calls from Saugerties village officials for a moratorium on such projects. Hirsch’s pledge of strict compliance with the state’s Open Meetings Law comes after opponents of the Key Capture project in Saugerties accused a town zoning working group, whose meetings are not open to the public, of being out of compliance with the state law. Key Capture and Ulster County are also proposing a lithium-ion battery storage facility at the site of the county’s under-construction emergency communications center on Paradies Lane in the town of New Paltz.

artigo.texto: The Volusia County Council on Tuesday, Oct. 6, held the first of two required public hearings on a proposed ordinance to prohibit large-scale data centers in unincorporated Volusia County, continuing a process that began in August to address community concerns about water resources, infrastructure, energy demand, and compatibility with surrounding communities. This is the latest step in a process that began Aug. 17, when council members directed staff to develop regulations addressing large-scale data centers, which State law defines as a facility at a single location with an anticipated monthly peak electrical load of 50 megawatts or more. The ordinance is scheduled to go before the Planning and Land Development Regulation Commission on Thursday, Oct. 15, then return to the county council for the second and final public hearing Tuesday, Oct. 20. If adopted after the final hearing, the ordinance would take effect upon filing with the Florida Department of State. No new applications The County has not accepted new applications for large-scale data centers in unincorporated Volusia County since Aug. 17, when the Council directed staff to pursue a prohibition. That hold will remain in place until the Council takes final action on the proposed ordinance. If ultimately adopted, the ordinance would make large-scale data centers prohibited use throughout unincorporated Volusia County. The county would not accept or process applications, development approvals, comprehensive plan amendments, rezonings, permits, site plans, or other County approvals associated with establishing, constructing, expanding, or operating a large-scale data center. The prohibition would apply only within unincorporated Volusia County and would not govern land-use decisions within municipalities.

artigo.texto: Mumbai: The Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking is set to roll out a new generation of Olectra Greentech electric buses in Mumbai. The buses are equipped with advanced Blade Battery technology, which is expected to offer a longer range and enhanced safety. The first batch of 25 buses is expected to become operational by the end of the month, The Times of India reported. The buses are equipped with lightweight batteries that will enable them to operate for up to two days on a single charge. Batteries designed to conserve energy The batteries use lithium iron phosphate technology and are integrated into the bus chassis. They are reported to be capable of storing at least 30 percent more energy compared with batteries installed in existing air-conditioned buses. The new buses are also designed to offer improved safety and a longer range while operating at lower costs. Olectra supplying buses to BEST Olectra Greentech Limited is supplying the Blade Battery-based electric buses to BEST as part of efforts to meet Mumbai's public transport requirements. Technology designed for enhanced safety A senior Olectra Greentech official was quoted as saying by The Times of India: “Blade battery is designed to withstand extreme climatic conditions and is much safer even when severely damaged during accidents. It has very slow heat generation and no oxygen release. It is also more compact, increasing space utilisation in the battery pack by over 50%." Buses equipped with the similar battery technology are also operating in other cities across the globe, including London and Singapore, according to the report. artigo.texto: Kenya is set to receive KSh590 million in European Union climate funding to strengthen the systems used to monitor, report and verify carbon-market activities and national climate action, as the country moves to establish a more structured framework for participating in international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The announcement was made in Nairobi on 5 October 2026 during the launch of the Kenya Guide for Strategic Engagement in Carbon Markets 2026, placing market integrity and institutional capacity at the centre of Kenya’s next phase of carbon-market development. EU Deputy Ambassador to Kenya Ondřej Šimíček said the funding, equivalent to about €4 million, would support Kenya’s monitoring, reporting and validation systems for both mitigation activities and national climate commitments. The support comes as Kenya seeks to create greater certainty for investors and project developers while ensuring that international transfers of carbon-related mitigation outcomes do not undermine the country’s own emissions-reduction commitments. The new Guide provides the institutional bridge between Kenya’s existing carbon-market regulations and the practical decisions required when projects seek to participate in international markets. Developed by the Government of Kenya with technical support from the Global Green Growth Institute’s Carbon Transaction Facility, it establishes principles, assessment criteria and implementation arrangements for evaluating and authorising carbon-market activities. It is intended to complement the Climate Change (Carbon Markets) Regulations, 2024, which provide Kenya’s underlying legal and institutional framework for carbon projects. One of the most significant elements of the framework is its approach to the volume of mitigation outcomes Kenya can authorise for international transfer. The Guide establishes a national carbon budget for trading, effectively placing a ceiling on the quantity of mitigation outcomes that can be transferred internationally while protecting the country’s ability to meet its Nationally Determined Contribution. Independent analysis of the July 2026 Guide puts the cumulative ceiling at approximately 10 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent through 2030. That limit is important because Article 6 transactions involve more than the sale of conventional carbon credits. Article 6.2 provides rules for countries cooperating through internationally transferred mitigation outcomes, or ITMOs, while requiring accounting arrangements designed to prevent double counting. Article 6.4 establishes a United Nations-supervised mechanism for generating and trading carbon credits, while Article 6.8 covers non-market approaches to international cooperation. For Kenya, this means the government must be able to determine which mitigation outcomes can be transferred abroad, record those transfers and account for them against its national climate commitments. The country’s 2024 carbon-market regulations already provide for authorisation of ITMO transfers and require corresponding adjustments where applicable. They also require transferred mitigation outcomes to be recorded in the National Carbon Registry. The development of the registry has consequently become an important component of Kenya’s carbon-market architecture. The Kenya National Carbon Registry was formally launched in February 2026 and is designed to track, verify and manage carbon credits and internationally transferred mitigation outcomes. The registry is managed by the National Environment Management Authority (NEMA), which also serves as Kenya’s Designated National Authority for Article 6 and other carbon markets. The registry is intended to address one of the fundamental risks facing carbon markets: whether emissions reductions or removals can be uniquely identified, tracked and accounted for throughout their lifecycle. NEMA has said the registry will support transparency, prevent double counting and double issuance, and provide a national platform for recording carbon-market projects, authorisations and mitigation outcomes. The Guide adds another layer of decision-making by establishing clearer criteria for projects seeking government approval. It introduces a structured process for engagement and prioritises activities that align with Kenya’s climate and development objectives. The framework also places greater emphasis on environmental and social safeguards, stakeholder engagement, benefit sharing and the broader value that carbon projects can create beyond the sale of credits. That shift has implications for the investment market. Carbon projects are increasingly being assessed not only according to the number of credits they can potentially generate, but also according to whether their emissions reductions are measurable, additional, traceable and compatible with national climate policy. Weak monitoring systems or uncertain ownership and accounting rules can increase transaction risks and make international buyers more cautious. For Kenya, strengthening monitoring, reporting and verification therefore has an economic dimension. Credible systems can reduce uncertainty for investors, improve the ability of buyers to assess projects and provide government with stronger oversight of mitigation activities taking place within its borders. The EU funding announced in Nairobi is intended to strengthen precisely these institutional capabilities. The development also builds on a longer Kenya-EU climate partnership. European support has been directed towards renewable energy, climate resilience, sustainable agriculture and climate-governance systems, while Kenya has been developing its own institutional capacity for carbon-market participation. The EU has also supported wider climate and green-growth initiatives that seek to mobilise private investment alongside public and development finance. artigo.texto: CATL World's largest battery manufacturer According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Advanced Energy Storage Systems market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global Advanced Energy Storage Systems market is undergoing a structural transformation from a policy-supported niche to a demand-pull cornerstone of modern energy infrastructure. As renewable penetration rises and grid operators confront intermittency, the economic case for storage has shifted from subsidy-driven to necessity-driven. Between 2026 and 2035, the market will be shaped by the imperative to integrate variable renewables, defer transmission upgrades, and enhance grid resilience. System integration and power conversion subsystems are emerging as critical value capture points, often determining project bankability more than the storage medium itself. A fundamental bifurcation is occurring: short-duration, high-cyclicity applications compete on $/kW and $/kWh metrics, while long-duration and resilience applications compete on total cost of ownership, safety, and site-specific integration complexity. Supply chain resilience has become a baseline requirement, and qualification burdens for new chemistries create time-to-market disadvantages. Procurement is shifting from component purchasing to performance-guaranteed, service-based contracts, forcing manufacturers to assume long-term operational risk. Geographic specialization is intensifying, creating complex trade dependencies. Safety protocols are evolving from afterthoughts to primary design constraints, influencing insurance, permitting, and deployment feasibility. This report provides a structured, commercially grounded analysis of these dynamics, offering decision-makers a clear view of deployment demand, technology positioning, manufacturing exposure, project economics, and competitive structure through 2035. The baseline scenario for the Advanced Energy Storage Systems market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates robust expansion, driven by the accelerating integration of renewable energy sources and the urgent need to modernize aging grid infrastructure. As solar and wind capacity grows, the intermittency challenge becomes more acute, making storage an indispensable component of reliable power systems. Utilities and grid operators are increasingly procuring storage to defer costly transmission and distribution upgrades, provide frequency regulation, and enhance resilience against extreme weather events. The commercial and industrial sector is also emerging as a significant demand center, motivated by energy cost management, sustainability targets, and the need for backup power. Technological advancements, particularly in lithium-ion chemistry and power conversion systems, are driving down costs and improving performance, further bolstering the economic case. However, the market faces headwinds from supply chain constraints, particularly in critical minerals and battery cell manufacturing, which could temper growth in certain regions. Policy support remains a key enabler, but the trend is toward market-based mechanisms that reward storage for its grid services. The competitive landscape is expected to consolidate, with integrated system providers gaining share over component suppliers. By 2035, the market is projected to reach a significantly higher level of deployment, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15.2% from 2026 to 2035, and the market index (2025=100) rising to 420, reflecting a more than fourfold increase in market value. This outlook assumes no major disruptive technological shifts or severe geopolitical crises, but acknowledges that regional variations will persist based on policy environments and resource endowments. Electric utilities and grid operators represent the largest and fastest-growing end-use sector for advanced energy storage systems. The primary mechanism driving demand is the need to integrate increasing shares of variable renewable generation, such as solar and wind, while maintaining grid stability and reliability. As renewable penetration exceeds 30-40% in many regions, the intermittency challenge becomes critical, necessitating storage for frequency regulation, voltage support, and energy shifting. Utilities are also deploying storage to defer or avoid costly upgrades to transmission and distribution infrastructure, using storage as a non-wires alternative. Additionally, storage provides essential grid services like spinning reserve and black start capability. Through 2035, demand will be further propelled by the retirement of aging fossil fuel peaker plants, which storage can replace with cleaner, faster-responding capacity. Key demand-side indicators include renewable capacity additions, grid interconnection queue volumes, and capacity market prices. The trend is toward larger, longer-duration projects, with utilities increasingly procuring storage through competitive solicitations and power purchase agreements. However, the pace of deployment varies by region, depending on regulatory frameworks and market designs that value storage's multiple benefits. Current trend: Rapid growth driven by renewable integration and grid modernization. Major trends: Shift from pilot projects to large-scale, multi-hundred-megawatt deployments, Increasing use of storage as a non-wires alternative to defer transmission upgrades, Growth in long-duration storage procurement to address seasonal variations, Integration of storage with renewable generation in hybrid projects, and Adoption of performance-based contracts and capacity markets. Representative participants: NextEra Energy, Duke Energy, Southern Company, National Grid, Enel, and Iberdrola. artigo.texto: Carbon tax deferment gives ministry more time to finalise regulatory, policy framework, says Arthur KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The deferment of the carbon tax implementation is aligned with the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry’s efforts to establish a complete regulatory and policy framework before enforcing emission caps. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the government decided to delay the tax, originally planned for this year, following global geopolitical developments that led to volatile energy prices, providing affected industries with a necessary buffer. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. That’s why we’ve been successful in launching the National Carbon Market Policy and I hope that we can table the Climate Change Act soon. “Once that is up, then we have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including the regulation, enforcement, the regulatory powers to give us to set the emission ceiling, and then we can know anything above the ceiling, then the carbon tax will come into place as a penalty to the polluters. “So, we’re not looking at this year for the carbon tax,” he said. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. He added that while operators need adequate time for feasibility studies and modifications, strict progress is required to qualify for temporary extensions. The session, titled “Building A Resilient Malaysia: Environment, Climate And Our Future”, was moderated by Bernama chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai. Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, as well as members of the local and foreign media based in Malaysia. artigo.texto: O satélite do Google subiu em 1º de outubro num Falcon 9 da SpaceX, o mesmo foguete que levou dois satélites feitos por alunos de escolas públicas do Brasil. É o primeiro teste em órbita do plano de montar data center movido a luz do Sol. O satélite do Google com quatro chips de inteligência artificial já está em órbita e respondendo. O protótipo do Project Suncatcher subiu na quinta-feira (1º) na missão Transporter-18 da SpaceX, e a empresa confirmou o contato no mesmo dia, em post assinado por Travis Beals, diretor do projeto. Segundo ele, a nave está “operando como esperado”. O aparelho foi construído em parceria com a Planet, empresa de imagens de satélite. A pergunta que ele precisa responder é simples de escrever e difícil de provar: um chip feito para data center em terra aguenta o espaço? O que o satélite do Google leva a bordo O protótipo tem quatro TPU, as unidades de processamento tensorial que o Google desenha para aprendizado de máquina e já usa nos próprios data centers. Segundo a NPR, os chips vão rodar uma versão do Gemma, o modelo aberto da empresa, para responder perguntas simples. Cada sessão dura 15 minutos, por limite de calor. - Computador raro Q1 de 1972 é encontrado sob caixas em casa de Londres, revela tecnologia Intel 8008 anterior ao Apple 1 e acaba vendido por mais de R$ 260 mil - Pesquisa brasileira mostra novo caminho para acelerar produção sustentável de amônia que pode ajudar a tornar mais eficientes processos industriais ligados aos fertilizantes agrícolas - Cientistas brasileiros usam drones e inteligência artificial para encontrar milho tolerante à seca e alcançam mais de 90% de acerto em parte dos testes - Volvo coloca VNL autônomo na rota Dallas–Houston, usa direção nível SAE 4 e mira escala com rede de 38 mil clientes para mudar o transporte de cargas nos EUA A NPR descreve o satélite do Google como do tamanho de uma geladeira. Ele fica numa órbita heliossíncrona, em que os painéis solares quase nunca entram na sombra. Isso dispensa baterias pesadas e energia de reserva. A meta é que a missão funcione por um ano. O próprio Beals chamou o voo de “um teste muito mínimo”. Primeiro a Planet coloca a nave para funcionar. Depois o Google liga as TPU do satélite e mede como elas se comportam com radiação, vibração e calor. Os números que o Google já mediu em terra Antes de o satélite do Google subir, a equipe publicou os testes de bancada. Eles ajudam a entender o tamanho do desafio: - Energia: na órbita certa, um painel solar rende até 8 vezes mais do que na superfície da Terra. - Lançamento: a subida dura cerca de 10 minutos, com cargas de até 10 g. Componentes isolados, como as TPU, podem sentir de 50 a 100 g. - Radiação: o chip Trillium (TPU v6e) foi testado num feixe de prótons de 67 MeV. A memória HBM só mostrou falhas depois de 2 krad(Si). A dose esperada em cinco anos de missão, com blindagem, é de 750 rad(Si). - Dose máxima: nenhuma falha permanente apareceu até 15 krad(Si), o maior valor testado num único chip. - Laser entre satélites: um demonstrador de bancada passou 800 Gbps em cada sentido, ou 1,6 Tbps no total, com um único par de transceptores. A conta da radiação mostra a folga. Dividindo 2.000 rad por 750 rad, o primeiro sinal de falha veio com 2,7 vezes a dose de cinco anos. Já os 15 krad sem dano permanente equivalem a 20 vezes essa dose. Os dados estão no post técnico do Google Research, de novembro de 2025, e o trabalho agora saiu revisado por pares na revista Joule. O problema do calor no vácuo Em terra, data center se resfria com ar ou água. Em órbita não existe ar. No vácuo, o calor só sai por radiadores, e por isso as sessões do Gemma ficam limitadas a 15 minutos. No satélite do Google, a saída testada é uma combinação de tubos de calor e radiadores. O conjunto passou por uma câmara de vácuo térmico, que imita o frio e o vácuo do espaço. Beals contou à NPR que os radiadores estão entre as peças mais pesadas do satélite do Google. Isso pesa no custo, porque cada quilo a mais encarece o lançamento. Brandon Lucia, professor de engenharia da Universidade Carnegie Mellon, lembrou outro ponto à NPR. Quando um chip quebra em um data center comum, um técnico entra e troca. Em órbita, segundo ele, custo e complexidade de manutenção sobem 10 ou até 100 vezes. Do protótipo à constelação de data center O satélite do Google é só o começo. A empresa imagina grupos de satélites voando muito perto uns dos outros, ligados por laser, cada um com dezenas de TPU. No modelo publicado, um aglomerado de 81 satélites voa a 650 km de altitude, num raio de 1 km. A distância entre vizinhos oscila entre 100 e 200 metros. A conta que decide o projeto é o preço por quilo. O Google calcula que o lançamento pode cair para menos de US$ 200 por quilo em meados da década de 2030. Nesse patamar, montar e operar um data center em órbita ficaria parecido com a conta de energia de um data center equivalente em terra, por quilowatt ao ano. O próximo passo é em 2027, com dois satélites em órbita para testar o laser entre eles. O próprio Beals freia a expectativa. Ele disse à NPR que não vê o modelo ficando mais barato nos próximos cinco anos. O mesmo foguete levou satélites de escolas brasileiras O Falcon 9 da Transporter-18 decolou da Base da Força Espacial de Vandenberg, na Califórnia, com 130 cargas. Entre elas estavam o EduSat-2 e o EduSat-3, montados por alunos de escolas públicas de Sorocaba (SP) e Fortaleza (CE). Os dois saíram do projeto AEB Escola em Órbita, da Agência Espacial Brasileira com a empresa Ideia Space. Em Sorocaba, a missão definida pelos alunos foi olhar para alagamentos e falhas de conectividade na região. A carona coletiva explica a mistura. Num voo desse tipo, a SpaceX divide o espaço do foguete entre dezenas de clientes, de gigantes da tecnologia a projetos de escola.

artigo.texto: Tesla deliveries top consensus, but energy storage deployments miss estimates Published: 12:40 05 Oct 2026 EDT Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA) delivered 487,000 vehicles in the third quarter, beating consensus estimates by 5% and extending the rebound in vehicle deliveries, according to UBS Securities. The electric vehicle maker’s deliveries rose 1% from the previous quarter but fell 2% year on year, with Model 3 and Model Y deliveries increasing 2% quarter on quarter and declining 1% year on year. UBS maintained its 'neutral' rating on Tesla and a $385 price target. UBS said the delivery result was positive, although expectations among investors had risen ahead of the release and may have reached 470,000 to 490,000 vehicles. The analyst said Tesla’s vehicle deliveries remained strong in some newer markets and exports, supported by production from its Shanghai facility. Tesla produced 464,000 vehicles in the quarter, up 3% from the previous quarter and 4% year on year, leaving production below deliveries and reducing estimated inventory days to 18 from 22. The weaker element of the release was energy storage, with deployments of 13.7 gigawatt-hours, up 1% quarter on quarter and 10% year on year but below the 15.9 gigawatt-hours consensus estimate. UBS said energy deployments were lumpy and difficult to forecast, but the shortfall could have a modest impact on its model because the business generates above-average gross margins. The analyst estimated the energy miss could reduce earnings by about $0.03, all else equal, leaving the overall delivery release with a mix of positive and negative factors.

artigo.texto: Companies Strengthen Position in Data Center Market Through Long-Term Chiller Partnership Supporting More Than 5GW of AI Data Center Capacity News Summary - LG Electronics has secured a long-term supply agreement with AIR Control Concepts to provide advanced cooling solutions for AI data centers in North America. - The agreement supports a large-scale, multi-year chiller supply program supporting data centers with more than 5GW of capacity. - This milestone reflects AIR's confidence in LG's cooling technologies to meet the demanding standards required for hyperscale data center infrastructure, positioning LG as a key supplier in this market. - For AIR, the partnership reinforces its position as one of North America's fastest-growing AI data center infrastructure platforms. NORFOLK, Va., Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics USA has signed a major supply agreement with AIR Control Concepts (AIR), the largest global platform of leading HVAC, electrical, service, and controls companies, to provide advanced chillers for data centers in the United States and Canada. The long-term contract builds on AIR's role as a leading AI data center (AIDC) platform provider and accelerates LG's expansion into the global AIDC cooling market, addressing the rapidly growing demand for high-efficiency thermal management solutions in AI infrastructure. Securing AI Infrastructure Partnership with Leading Data Center Developers Under the agreement, LG will supply advanced chillers supporting large-scale AI data center projects exceeding 5GW of capacity in North America. AIR oversees mega-scale infrastructure projects across major North American data center hubs, serving leading global data center operators as key customers. The LG Air-Cooled Centrifugal Chiller designed for AI data centers incorporates refrigerant free-cooling technology, using cool outdoor air to lower the compressor cooling load. Based on LG's internal simulation, refrigerant free-cooling can consume approximately 30 percent less energy annually than waterside free-cooling.1 This contract demonstrates that LG's cooling solutions meet AIR's stringent technical and reliability requirements for its hyperscale data center projects. Moving beyond single-project bids, the agreement establishes LG as a core infrastructure partner supporting the growth of AI data centers in North America. For AIR, the partnership reinforces its position as one of North America's fastest-growing AI data center infrastructure platforms. As data center customers race to bring new capacity online, AIR is scaling the operational depth and supplier relationships needed to deliver mission-critical cooling infrastructure on schedule and at the standard the industry now requires. Targeting Rapid Growth in the Global AIDC Market The expansion of LG's AI data center cooling business draws on six decades of HVAC engineering experience in high-reliability environments such as nuclear power plants and large hospitals. Building on recent successes in supplying cooling solutions to hyperscale AI data centers in North America, LG is also expanding its global footprint with key data center projects in the Middle East and Indonesia. By leveraging the integrated capabilities of the broader LG Group to offer comprehensive cooling solutions, the company aims to drive mid- to long-term revenue growth. The global AI data center market presents significant growth opportunities. According to Fortune Business Insights, the market is expected to grow by approximately 26 percent annually, reaching $133.5 billion by 2034. In its second-quarter 2026 earnings report, LG highlighted that first-half orders for data center cooling solutions exceeded $428 million, and the company expects orders to reach several billion dollars by year-end. The company expects to achieve its 2027 chiller business revenue target of approximately $680 million (1 trillion Korean won) ahead of schedule.2 Leveraging Complementary Capabilities to Address Exploding Demand "This agreement reflects the confidence data center customers place in AIR to deliver mission-critical infrastructure at a scale and pace the industry has never seen before," said Brad Hobbs, Chief Executive Officer of AIR Control Concepts. "LG's high-efficiency chiller technology gives us a proven platform we can deploy with confidence across our AI data center portfolio, and this agreement positions AIR to support our customers' growth for years to come." "As heat management in AI data centers emerges as a major global priority, LG aims to be a major player in the global AIDC cooling market," said James Lee, president of the LG Electronics ES Company. "We will achieve this through our differentiated technology, including our high-efficiency chillers, and our rapidly expanding experience in supplying leading big tech companies." "We're excited to deepen our partnership with LG at exactly the moment our industry needs it most," said Hayden Bland, President of AIR Control Concepts. "Data center operators are looking for partners who can deliver mission-critical reliability, capacity and certainty at scale. Together with LG, we're building the technology, manufacturing capacity and support infrastructure to meet that need. For data center customers planning their next generation of infrastructure, now is the time to engage with us." "Data center cooling represents a key pillar of LG's global growth strategy, and this major supply agreement with AIR marks an inflection point for LG's North American chiller business," said Don Kwack, CEO, LG Electronics North America. "This alliance leverages LG's proven cooling innovations and AIR's strong position with U.S. data center developers at a critical time for reliable AI infrastructure expansion." 1 Based on LG's internal simulation of a single 1,750 kW unit operating at 100 percent cooling capacity under climate conditions in the Seoul metropolitan area. The company bid in partnership with Madhav Infra Projects Ltd, which emerged as the L1 bidder for Cluster C of UPCL's tender under the tariff-based competitive bidding mechanism, JWL said in a statement. The projects involve supply and commissioning of BESS systems worth about ₹100 crore. JWL has also received the formal Letter of Award from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Ltd (WBSEDCL) for a 50 MW/200 MWh standalone BESS project at the Jeerat 132 kV substation in North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal. The project was secured in August 2026. Substation-level storage of the kind being deployed in Uttarakhand and West Bengal is central to the framework, and JEM Energy is building its utility-scale portfolio in line with it, it added. "Winning the Uttarakhand project and receiving the formal award for Jeerat are important steps in building JEM Energy into a scalable energy storage business," JWL Managing Director Vivek Lohia said. The company reiterated its target of building a BESS order book of about ₹1,000 crore by FY27. "As the business scales, we expect Jupiter Electric Mobility (JEM) to turn EBITDA positive in Q3 FY27 and to turn profitable by FY28. We will continue to bid with discipline for utility-scale and Commercial & Industrial (C&I) opportunities across India," Lohia said.

artigo.texto: The Vandalia City Council moves forward with the process of eventually approving an ordinance for Battery Energy Storage Systems. During their meeting on Monday night, the Vandalia City Council discussed the matter and was probably their longest topic of discussion during Monday’s meeting. Alderman Kenny Lewey asked some questions about the need for the ordinance and City Attorney Ryan Connor and Mayor Doug Knebel this gets the ball rolling on the matter for the City of Vandalia. Mayor Knebel says, at this time with no ordinance in place, a company would not be able to put in a Battery Energy Storage System in Vandalia. Alderman Russ Stunkel asked if this is a matter where the City is getting their hand forced by the State and he got further explanation from Connor and City Administrator LaTisha Paslay on the matter. The matter was approved by the Vandalia City Council by a 5 to 2 vote with Aldermen Mike Hobler and Steve Barker voting No and Alderman Ken Hubler absent from the meeting. The ordinance will now be referred off to the Planning & Zoning Committee for review. After their review of the matter and possible changes, it would then come back to the Vandalia City Council for final approval.

artigo.texto: Notícias RESOLUÇÃO Custeio de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias entra em consulta A minuta de resolução sobre a base de custeio e a metodologia de rateio do Encargo de Reserva de Capacidade associado à contratação de Sistemas de Armazenamento de Energia em baterias (Ercap-SAE) é tema da Consulta Pública nº 37/2026 e de workshop, conforme aprovado na 20ª Reunião Pública Ordinária da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (ANEEL), na terça-feira (06/10). É importante ressaltar que a proposta trata exclusivamente do Ercap-SAE e não dispõe sobre o Encargo de Reserva de Capacidade Geral (Ercap-Geral), pretendendo assegurar que os dois regimes coexistam sem sobreposição. A proposta de regulação busca garantir a sustentabilidade econômica dos projetos de armazenamento, essenciais para a expansão contínua das fontes renováveis variáveis na matriz elétrica nacional. Pela minuta, estarão sujeitos ao rateio do Ercap-SAE os titulares de outorga ou de registro de central geradora que se enquadrem como agentes da Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE), excluindo a Micro e Minigeração Distribuída (MMGD) e o armazenamento autônomo. Está previsto, ainda, que a base de cálculo do encargo seja a energia efetivamente associada a cada agente de geração no período de apuração e que caberá ao Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) divulgar anualmente a classificação dos empreendimentos para aplicação no ano subsequente. Ainda pela minuta, o Ercap-SAE integrará a estrutura de financiamento da reserva de capacidade junto à Conta de Potência para Reserva de Capacidade (CONCAP). Como participar A Consulta Pública nº 37/2026 terá duração de 30 dias, de 08/10/2026 a 06/11/2026, quando poderão ser enviados subsídios e informações adicionais para o e-mail cp037_2026@aneel.gov.br. Os documentos que integram o processo, incluindo a Análise de Impacto Regulatório (AIR) e a minuta de resolução, estão disponíveis no portal da ANEEL, no menu Participação Social > Consultas Públicas. Durante o período da consulta, a ANEEL promoverá um workshop para apresentação da proposta e discussão da metodologia de rateio, dos índices e patamares de flexibilidade, dos critérios de enquadramento, da segregação entre o Ercap-Geral e o Ercap-SAE e dos mecanismos de apuração, repasse e liquidação. A data será oportunamente divulgada. O evento estará aberto à participação dos agentes setoriais, da Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE), do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) e aos demais interessados.

artigo.texto: Finlândia freia construção de dois 'data centers' da Google por impacto ambiental Empresa responsável por obras não teria apresentado reltório de avaliação; agência do governo investiga corte de mais de 300 hectares de floresta Uma agência governamental finlandesa ordenou, nesta terça-feira (6), que a Google suspenda a construção de novos "data centers" em dois municípios da Finlândia no mais tardar em 23 de outubro de 2026, à espera de uma avaliação de seu impacto ambiental. Estes projetos fazem parte de um investimento de 13 bilhões de euros (R$ 72,7 bilhões) anunciado na Finlândia, o maior investimento da gigante tecnológica americana na Europa no âmbito da inteligência artificial. Durante uma visita na semana passada à cidade de Muhos, uma jornalista da AFP observou o ir e vir de retroescavadeiras. Em frente à fazenda de um dos moradores com quem conversou, a floresta tinha desaparecido de um terreno adquirido pela Google. - Caribe em Ipanema: Descoberta de bancos de algas calcárias cor-de-rosa surpreende pesquisadores; veja - Quer morar fora? Guia reúne informações sobre 36 países A agência finlandesa de supervisão exigiu, em um comunicado, que sejam suspensas "todas as medidas preparatórias suscetíveis de modificar de forma significativa o meio ambiente no âmbito dos projetos de 'data centers' previstos em Muhos e Kajaani", no noroeste do país. A agência abriu uma investigação pela suspeita de que a empresa Tuike Finland, que representa a Google, cortou mais de 300 hectares de floresta em Muhos sem realizar previamente a avaliação de impacto ambiental. As obras devem ser interrompidas até que seja feita esta avaliação, detalhou a agência. "Entendemos as preocupações expressas e reconhecemos que, neste caso concreto, não estivemos à altura de nossos próprios padrões, que são elevados", admitiu Sondre Ronander, porta-voz da Google, em uma mensagem enviada à AFP. "Estudaremos as conclusões da agência e seguiremos suas recomendações", acrescentou. Graças a um clima ameno, uma eletricidade relativamente estável e barata, produzida majoritariamente mediante energia nuclear, além de uma ampla capacidade eólica e hidrelétrica, a Finlândia experimentou recentemente um auge dos investimentos em "data centers".

artigo.texto: Geral Aneel aprova consulta pública sobre custeio da contratação de baterias no sistema elétrico Consulta pública ficará aberta até 9 de novembro de 2026 A diretoria da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) decidiu nesta terça-feira, 6, abrir consulta pública de 30 dias para o aprimoramento da proposta de custeio da contratação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, na modalidade de reserva de capacidade. A consulta ficará aberta de 8 de outubro a 9 de novembro de 2026. A área técnica da Agência apontou, em parecer de agosto, que a melhor alternativa para os custos da contratação de baterias é o rateio entre todos os geradores de energia. Contudo, a proposta é que o pagamento seja modulado em função do chamado Índice de Flexibilidade (IF). Com esse critério, aquelas usinas com maior flexibilidade pagariam menos (25% do encargo), enquanto aquelas com menor flexibilidade pagariam 100%. A alternativa, ainda de acordo com a área técnica, apresenta o “melhor equilíbrio” entre a aderência à finalidade do encargo, a estabilidade do custeio, a objetividade técnica e a viabilidade regulatória. O tema é controverso, especialmente porque há projetos de lei no Congresso buscando derrubar essa previsão de rateio dos custos. A Lei nº 15.269/2025, de modernização do setor elétrico, previu expressamente que os custos decorrentes da contratação de baterias sejam rateados apenas entre os geradores de energia elétrica, excluindo a possibilidade de custeio pelos consumidores. Os dois leilões de baterias, inéditos, estão previstos para dezembro deste ano. O diretor Gentil Nogueira, relator, comentou que a proposta em discussão trata da “norma perene”, que, se aprovada, poderá ser utilizada para o custeio dos sistemas de armazenamento que devem ser contratados no leilão de baterias marcado para dezembro. No entanto, ele salientou que o próprio edital do leilão, ainda a ser aprovado, pode trazer disciplina para esse custeio específico. O edital precisa ser aprovado até o fim de outubro, de maneira a cumprir a regra de publicação com 30 dias de antecedência. artigo.texto: The Cap Times is an independent newsroom serving Madison and Wisconsin. Sign up for the Morning Update to receive news in your inbox each morning. While state lawmakers and both candidates in Wisconsin’s race for governor say they want individual communities to have the final say in data center development, local policymakers say that approach puts them in a tricky position. Dane County communities, including Madison and the county itself, have passed temporary moratoriums on data center development amid public opposition to the facilities. In Sun Prairie, which passed a moratorium on facilities of 10,000 square feet or larger in September, the city’s Utilities Commission received its first public comment on any topic in five years, commission chair Josh Christensen announced to the delight of its members. The topic was data centers, and resident Jenna Frost wanted to put in her two cents in a written comment in August. “She strongly wanted us to know that she is in support of a moratorium, would like to see transparency throughout any process and is very anti-data center,” Christensen said in summary. Public speculation about possible data center developments has also mounted. During a recent Sun Prairie City Council meeting, Mayor Steve Stocker asked staff members to dispel a rumor that the city’s proposal to acquire nearby marshland would pave the way for a data center. Property zoned for parkland can’t be developed. But whispers about possible data centers aren’t exactly unfounded. The state is home to at least 30 data centers, a report from the Wisconsin Policy Forum found. While most are older and smaller facilities, the state has seen growing interest in so-called “hyperscale” facilities from big technology companies like Microsoft, Oracle and Open AI. Seven such proposals, including a $12 billion facility near DeForest, have been blocked at the local level, but others, like those in Port Washington and Beaver Dam, have continued. Mike Peters, president of the nonprofit power provider WPPI Energy, recounted a meeting last fall when he asked the utility’s board members from the 51 communities WPPI serves whether they had been approached by data centers. “Half the hands went up in the room,” Peters said. “Data centers are out there knocking on the door of most of our members.” Often, they’re doing so quietly. Patrick Miles, chair of the Dane County Board, sponsored the resolution that set up an 18-month moratorium on hyperscale data center development in areas where the county has zoning authority, in large part as a way of creating transparency in an often opaque process. “Learning about their habit of using NDAs (non-disclosure agreements) when they’re talking with community decisionmakers, it’s no wonder that there’s so much distrust and concern,” Miles said. “It started becoming clear to me that we’re living in the Wild West. There aren’t guidelines. There aren’t guardrails.” The nature of the current data center prospecting and development process is frustrating local elected officials. Cynthia Richson, chair of Middleton’s Town Board, called it a “playbook” where well-resourced companies privately reach out to local officials to “one by one turn them.” “They like local officials who don’t know much because they’re kind of easy to persuade when you dangle a big pile of money in front of them, which is sad,” said Richson, who serves on Dane County’s Advisory Committee on Data Centers. “‘Taking advantage’ seems like how I would describe that (tactic) of sophisticated tech people.” Local officials have some tools at their disposal to regulate data center development. Both Richson and Madison City Council member Derek Field, who sits on the city’s Plan Commission, pointed to long-range planning and zoning as the primary way communities can limit or prohibit the facilities. Still, finding answers amid what Field called “the biggest land use discussion of our time” is challenging for local lawmakers in Wisconsin because of the pace of changing technology, a relative lack of reliable information, and an inability to act more broadly. Local leaders have also found themselves somewhat at odds with state lawmakers’ current approach to the issue, especially as the Legislature created a set of tax exemptions for data center developers in 2023. “I’m under no delusion that a (hypothetical) hyperscale data center that opens on the town of Cottage Grove side of our municipal boundary would have any less of an impact on the power rates we have to pay for the next 30 years,” Field said. “This is definitely a regional problem. I think we are struggling to figure out how to deal with those impacts locally when we can only legislate within Madison.” While the county’s task force started as a way of advising Dane County communities on data centers, Miles said it’s taken on an informal lobbying role. “What has evolved in this is also a need to (reach) another audience — state government — for us to identify gaps and weaknesses in state policy,” Miles said. ‘A significant disadvantage’ At a recent meeting of the county task force, Jim Hamilton, executive director of the Nuclear Decommissioning Collaborative, drew comparisons between nuclear power plants and hyperscale data centers, given the amount of land required, environmental questions, payment structures to local governments, and the need to retire equipment after a certain period of time. He advised members to “get everything up front” in agreements with developers so local communities aren’t left to pay for future costs when the payments stop. In Wisconsin, local governments cannot mandate developers to sign community benefit agreements that can require, for example, the use of union labor or renewable power sourcing as part of a conditional use permitting process. artigo.texto: Mercado global de baterias de base biológica: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado global de baterias de base biológica até 2035: crescimento impulsionado por metas corporativas de ESG e aplicações críticas de segurança Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de baterias de base biológica, o mercado entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de baterias de base biológica está deixando a fase de validação em laboratório para entrar na implantação comercial inicial, abrindo nichos defensáveis em que biodegradabilidade, não toxicidade e segurança reforçada compensam as atuais limitações de densidade energética e potência. Diferentemente da cadeia de suprimentos intensiva em minerais das baterias de íons de lítio, os gargalos críticos desse mercado estão no fornecimento de bio-precursores de alta pureza, como celulose, quitosana e lignina, e no estabelecimento de rotas de bioprocessamento escaláveis. A demanda se divide entre aplicações sensíveis a custo e de grande volume, como embalagens inteligentes e eletrônicos descartáveis, e segmentos premium, como implantes médicos e sensores ambientais, em que credenciais de segurança e sustentabilidade justificam um prêmio de preço. A integração de sistemas continua sendo um obstáculo, pois as células de base biológica frequentemente exigem sistemas de gerenciamento de bateria sob medida, adaptados aos seus perfis únicos de carga e descarga. Os ventos regulatórios favoráveis do REACH e das restrições a PFAS são contrabalançados pela ausência de padrões de desempenho unificados, o que retarda a qualificação junto a compradores avessos ao risco. Os papéis geográficos vão se cristalizando, com regiões fortes em biotecnologia emergindo como polos de P&D e mercados com regras ambientais rigorosas formando os primeiros núcleos de demanda. Este relatório analisa o mercado de 2012 a 2025 e projeta o período até 2035, oferecendo uma visão estruturada da demanda de implantação, do posicionamento tecnológico e da dinâmica competitiva. O cenário-base para o mercado de baterias de base biológica até 2035 prevê uma transição da prototipagem de nicho para a comercialização em escala, embora o crescimento permaneça concentrado em aplicações especializadas, e não na substituição massiva das baterias de íons de lítio. Espera-se que o mercado cresça a uma taxa composta de crescimento anual de 8,2% entre 2026 e 2035, alcançando um índice de mercado de 220 em 2035 (2025=100). Esse crescimento se apoia em três forças estruturais: primeiro, o endurecimento das regulamentações ambientais sobre descarte de baterias e materiais perigosos, sobretudo na Europa e na América do Norte, obrigará os fabricantes de equipamentos originais a buscar alternativas para dispositivos de baixa potência e descartáveis; segundo, as metas corporativas de ESG impulsionarão a compra de soluções de armazenamento sustentáveis para redes de IoT, monitoramento ambiental e energia de reserva em locais sensíveis; e terceiro, aplicações críticas de segurança nos setores médico, de defesa e em instalações protegidas adotarão químicas de base biológica onde os riscos de fuga térmica das baterias convencionais são inaceitáveis. No entanto, o cenário-base não pressupõe nenhum avanço na densidade energética que torne as baterias de base biológica competitivas para armazenamento em escala na rede ou para veículos elétricos antes de 2035. O desenvolvimento da cadeia de suprimentos se concentrará em garantir bio-precursores consistentes e de alta pureza e em escalar o bioprocessamento, com a Ásia-Pacífico liderando na fabricação e a Europa na demanda impulsionada por regulação. Os preços permanecerão com prêmio em relação às baterias de íons de lítio na maioria dos segmentos, justificado pela economia no descarte ao fim da vida útil e pelos benefícios de segurança. O mercado segue vulnerável à volatilidade dos preços das matérias-primas e à falta de padrões de desempenho unificados, o que pode atrasar ciclos de qualificação e retardar a adoção em setores regulados. Vetores e restrições da demanda Principais vetores de demanda - Metas corporativas de ESG e de pegada de carbono impulsionando a compra de soluções de armazenamento sustentáveis - Regulamentações ambientais rigorosas sobre descarte de baterias e materiais perigosos (por exemplo, REACH e restrições a PFAS) - Demanda por aplicações críticas de segurança, nas quais os riscos de fuga térmica das baterias convencionais são proibitivos - Crescimento das redes de IoT e do monitoramento ambiental, que exigem baterias de baixa potência, longa duração, descartáveis ou biodegradáveis - Avanços em bioprocessamento e química verde reduzindo custos de produção e melhorando o desempenho dos materiais - Aumento dos custos de descarte ao fim da vida útil das baterias convencionais, criando incentivo econômico para alternativas biodegradáveis Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - Densidade energética e potência menores em comparação com as baterias de íons de lítio, limitando o uso em aplicações de alto desempenho - Ausência de padrões unificados de desempenho e segurança específicos para químicas de base biológica, aumentando as exigências de qualificação - Qualidade e oferta inconsistentes de bio-precursores de alta pureza, gerando gargalos de produção - Custos iniciais mais altos em relação às tecnologias incumbentes, apesar da economia no descarte no longo prazo - Disponibilidade limitada de sistemas de gerenciamento de bateria sob medida e de equipamentos de conversão de energia adaptados às células de base

artigo.texto: With a few dozen data centers already up and running in Pennsylvania and proposals on the table for over 100 more, public opposition is growing — especially to the new hyperscale projects intended to support AI. Like his counterparts across the Chesapeake Bay region, Gov. Josh Shapiro is reading the room. According to a Quinnipiac University poll released in July, 74% of Pennsylvania voters say they would be against building an AI data center in their community. And on Aug. 18, Shapiro signed an executive order intended to give municipalities more control over data center development and to establish stricter guardrails for those projects. Governors in Maryland and Virginia have since followed suit. Shapiro’s order is “an important way to address concerns about consumer impacts, environmental impacts and public health impacts from data centers,” said Robert Routh, the state’s policy director for the Natural Resources Defense Council. Shapiro, a Democrat, was once a champion for data center development. In June 2025, his administration announced a $20 billion Amazon investment for AI infrastructure in Pennsylvania. “Our team worked closely with local leaders and Amazon to land this deal,” he said at the time. But with public outcry growing and the number of proposals multiplying, the Shapiro administration is attempting to place checks on the industry. In a May 2026 precursor to the executive order, Shapiro’s team announced the Governor’s Responsible Infrastructure Development (GRID) initiative, intended to establish “strict standards that data centers must comply with to receive support from the commonwealth.” Those standards include commitments to economic development, energy affordability and transparency. They also address environmental protection, such as requirements for technologies that minimize water use and air pollution. In exchange, data center developers could expect speedier permitting through the PA Permit Fast Track Program. But compliance with GRID is voluntary. The new executive order adds teeth to the program and gives more power to local communities. Now, developers who sign a legally binding agreement with the state Department of Environmental Protection to meet GRID requirements can immediately submit permit applications for review. But DEP will not issue those permits until municipalities have approved the project. If a developer refuses to sign the agreement, DEP will not even begin reviewing its permit applications until local approval is secured. And the department will not issue any permits until all applications have been submitted. Developers who do not agree to GRID will also not qualify for the existing tax exemption on data center computer equipment. The order also removes all data center proposals from the PA Permit Fast Track Program, prohibits developers from using nondisclosure agreements and requires data center operators to report energy and water usage to DEP annually beginning in July 2027. “There are no AI data centers up-and-running right now in Pennsylvania,” Shapiro remarked at his executive order signing ceremony. And only two have completed DEP review, according to the department’s new Data Center Permit Tracker website. One of those is in Westmoreland County, and the other is one of two planned for Lancaster County. The expectation, one administration official said on background, is that these new requirements will help distinguish projects that may never be built from “projects that are serious, have financing and access to power and have a committed end user.” The order means that developers cannot use the state’s approval as leverage at the local level, said David Sanko, executive director of the Pennsylvania State Association of Township Supervisors. Developers, he adds, will no longer get their state permits first and then say, “Well, the state already says ‘okay.’ Why are you in the way?” Kirk Stoner, director of planning for Cumberland County, across the Susquehanna River west of Harrisburg, wishes the GRID guidance had come sooner. His county is home to the hotly contested $15 billion PAX-1 data center project in Middlesex Township. Some of the arguments over energy, water and air quality could have been more focused if there had been more definitive information on resource impacts to consider upfront, he said. But exactly how the executive order will play out in individual towns isn’t yet clear. “A lot of the ordinances that I’m seeing here in Cumberland County are really strict, and I’m not sure that there’s going to be a lot of projects moving forward to the state level,” Stoner said. A municipality might, for example, restrict data center development to a minimum lot size of 40 acres within an industrial zone that doesn’t contain available lots that size. Stoner said it begs the question, “At what point does the private sector and the data center industry start to push back on some of those and come in and challenge ordinances to say they’re exclusionary?” Stoner also wonders whether some municipalities might actually request that DEP complete reviews of environmental permits first, so they don’t waste time and concern citizens with projects that might ultimately be killed at the state level. Another question is how many data center developers will sign the GRID agreement. “In distinguishing speculative proposals from real projects, it’s important that rules are not changed midstream, impacting ongoing investment in verified and responsible data center projects,” said Dan Diorio, executive vice president of state policy and government affairs for the Data Center Coalition, a trade association. “Companies have made plans, [and] communities have prepared for economic opportunities.” As of September 18, one month after the executive order was signed, a Shapiro administration official told the Bay Journal thatno data center developers had signed on. artigo.texto: Tesla’s Q3 Deliveries Beat UBS’ Estimates — But Energy Storage Miss Keeps This Analyst Neutral - The automaker delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3, about 5% above UBS’ consensus, according to investing.com. - Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh of energy-storage products, up from 13.5 GWh in Q2 and 12.5 GWh a year earlier - The brokerage said buyside expectations had been rising ahead of the deliveries report. Tesla (TSLA) remained on investors’ radar on Monday after better-than-expected third-quarter deliveries last Friday, though UBS said the beat was partially offset by weaker energy storage deployments. At the time of writing, TSLA shares were up 2%. UBS Sees Sustained Rebound In Vehicle Deliveries Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter (Q3), about 5% above UBS’ consensus, according to investing.com. Model 3 and Model Y accounted for 478,237 of those deliveries. The EV maker also produced 464,391 vehicles during the quarter, including 457,387 Model 3 and Model Y units. Deliveries rose about 1.3% from the previous quarter, while production increased nearly 3%. However, deliveries were still about 2% below the same period last year, when Tesla posted its highest-ever quarterly deliveries. UBS said buyside expectations had been rising ahead of the deliveries report and noted that the latest numbers showed a continued rebound in vehicle deliveries. Energy Storage Comes In Below Expectations Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh of energy-storage products, up from 13.5 GWh in the second quarter (Q2) and 12.5 GWh a year earlier. Still, the figure came in below expectations. UBS said the energy business can be difficult to forecast because deployment timing is often uneven. Since the segment carries above-average gross margins, the shortfall is expected to have a small impact on its model, worth roughly $0.03, UBS said. The firm reiterated a ‘Neutral’ rating on Tesla with a $385 price target, implying around 1.7% upside from current levels. Analysts Still Split On The Bigger Picture Earlier, Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster said the delivery data suggested the “EV winter” may be thawing, but Ross Gerber, CEO and co-founder of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth and Investment Management, was more cautious, noting that Tesla’s current annualized delivery pace remains below 2 million vehicles. JPMorgan also said Q3 sales were better than expected, helped by markets outside the U.S. and China, including stronger trends in Europe. However, the firm kept its below-consensus estimates due to expectations for lower automotive gross margins and higher spending. It also maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating and kept its $415 price target unchanged. Retail’s Take On TSLA Retail sentiment surrounding TSLA on Stocktwits remained in the ‘bullish’ zone over the past 24 hours. One user expects the stock to run up to $420 ahead of its Q3 earnings on October 21. Another user expects the stock to climb to $384 by the next session if it breaks the $378.56 resistance. Despite the recent recovery, TSLA is down 13% so far in 2026 and is the only stock in the Magnificent 7 cohort trading in the red.
