artigo.texto: As AI moves from experimentation into production, data centers face growing demands for power, cooling, and space. Real-time inference and other AI workloads require infrastructure that can scale without adding unnecessary complexity. Conventional rack designs may not provide the density, or flexibility operators need, while proprietary designs can limit hardware choices and make expansion more complex. Cisco helps operators integrate and scale networking into ORv3 environments while maintaining a consistent operating model. What ORv3 changes for high-density AI data centers Open Rack Version 3 (ORv3) is designed for high-density environments. Developed through the Open Compute Project (OCP), it defines an open rack architecture with mechanical and serviceability specifications and supports power designs suited to modern AI, machine learning, and high-performance computing (HPC) systems. ORv3 racks use a 21-inch equipment bay and Open Units (OU); traditional enterprise equipment commonly uses 19-inch racks and Rack Units (RU). One OU measures 48 mm, while one RU measures 44.45 mm. Some ORv3 designs accommodate 19-inch equipment with mounting adapters, but rack dimensions and usable space vary. That flexibility can help organizations introduce high-density infrastructure while continuing to support compatible equipment and existing deployment strategies. The value of ORv3 comes down to efficiency and scale. ORv3 delivers several important advantages: - Standardized interoperability: Components from different manufacturers can work together more seamlessly, enabling a more open, plug-and-play approach and reducing concerns about hardware compatibility. - Higher power and cooling: A 48V DC busbar power distribution system can reduce power loss and support higher power densities compared to traditional designs. It also offers built-in support for direct liquid cooling (DLC) manifolds and blind-mate connections to manage the intense heat of AI servers. - Sustainability benefits: Reusable components and standardized hardware help reduce waste, lower carbon footprints, and minimize operational inefficiencies. - Operational Efficiency: Features tool-free, “click-in” assembly for IT gear and power rails, allowing for faster maintenance and reduced cabling complexity. It also supports hybrid mounting for both 21-inch OCP (OU) and traditional 19-inch (RU) equipment within the same frame. These features make ORv3 more than a rack specification. They offer a practical foundation for aligning infrastructure density, operational needs, and future growth. How Cisco is supporting the transition Cisco is preparing its data center networking portfolio for evolving rack designs. Cisco offers ORv3- compatible trays for Cisco N9000 Series switches. The trays align networking hardware with open-rack mechanical and power designs, giving operators more flexibility as they build or expand high-density data centers. Customers can choose a bundle with the switch preinstalled on the tray or purchase a spare tray for self-installation, depending on their deployment needs. Cisco N9000 ORv3 compliant trays for operational choice Key capabilities include: - Compatibility with ORv3 rack environments for Cisco N9000 Series switches. - Support for 48V DC power architectures aligned to modern high-density requirements. - Mounting kits for existing 19-inch equipment, enabling traditional gear to fit into the 21-inch ORv3 environment. Cisco power trays are designed to connect at different busbar positions, helping ensure the hardware receives the power it needs in supported rack configurations. This design readiness is essential in high-density environments, where small physical differences can have a significant operational impact. Together, these options give organizations a path to adopt ORv3-based infrastructure while maintaining continuity in network operations, accommodating compatible existing equipment, and aligning the rack with AI’s power, cooling, and density demands. Cisco accelerates AI infrastructure with new liquid-cooled switches: the ORv3-native N9364F-SG3-RL and the purpose-built N9164F-NS6-ML for NVIDIA MGX accelerated-computing rack deployments. These platforms deliver the critical thermal and connectivity efficiency required for modern, high-density AI fabrics. Cisco Nexus switches are part of Cisco Nexus One, a data center networking architecture for AI and modern workloads. With Cisco Cloud Control, Nexus One supports a unified AgenticOps experience for managing infrastructure from silicon to workloads. Who benefits most from an ORv3-ready approach ORv3 is especially relevant for hyperscale and enterprise data centers with roadmaps that include large-scale AI or machine learning workloads. For these organizations, the move to ORv3 is not simply about following the latest hardware standards. It is about creating a data center foundation that can scale with the performance, density, and efficiency requirements of modern workloads. - Simplify the deployment of a high-density fabric. - Maintain environmental goals as infrastructure grows. - Future proof existing investments and extend their longevity. - Reduce total cost of ownership. Building the foundation for what comes next As AI shifts into production and real-time inference, the physical design of the data center becomes a strategic consideration. ORv3 introduces an open, high-density architecture built for the power and thermal realities of AI, machine learning, and HPC. Cisco N9000 support for ORv3 helps organizations adopt that architecture with greater confidence, while preserving proven networking performance and management consistency. Data centers need a smarter, more scalable infrastructure foundation to support continued compute growth. artigo.texto: Enduro 4 smartwatch redefines ultraperformance with extreme battery life and advanced training features Comprehensive power modes, enhanced stamina metrics, a ComfortFit Fabric Band and Garmin Epic help endurance athletes and multiday adventurers train, race and explore even farther OLATHE, Kan. , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Garmin (NYSE: GRMN) today announced Enduro™ 4, its longest-lasting GPS smartwatch with solar charging, which includes dynamic features and capabilities to take endurance enthusiasts farther on their next expedition. Utilizing an energy-efficient 1.4" MIP display in combination with a solar lens, Enduro 4 has up to 320 hours of battery life in activity mode1 or up to 90 days of battery life in smartwatch mode2. It also leverages innovative updates like grade-adjusted pace-based workout targets, grade-adjusted rolling pace, stamina zones, stamina curve and Garmin Epic multiday activity logging. "As interest and participation in ultra-endurance activities continue to grow, Enduro 4 is designed for athletes and adventurers who want gear they can trust to perform through every mile, every climb and every challenge . Intuitive features like comprehensive power modes make the most of the long-lasting battery life, while grade-adjusted metrics add a new dimension to preparing for hilly or mountainous terrain." —Susan Lyman, Garmin Vice President of Consumer Sales and Marketing Grade-adjusted features, stamina metrics and more In addition to 100+ activity profiles, Enduro 4 introduces new capabilities to the Enduro line, optimized for trail runners, multiday hikers and backpackers, and endurance athletes. - Comprehensive power modes provide preset options to optimize battery life and performance based on the needs of the user. Configurations include Max Accuracy, which offers full-feature tracking for shorter efforts, and Max Battery, ideal for extended activity recording (up to 320 hours with solar charging). - Grade-adjusted pace-based workout targets help athletes maintain the right effort range on hilly terrain, while grade-adjusted rolling pace provides a real-time view of pace over varying terrain. - Stamina zones show athletes how their stamina impacts an activity, and stamina curve helps users understand how their endurance changes over time based on fitness and training history. - With 50% more RAM than Enduro 3 and a more powerful, updated map engine, navigation is easier than ever with 30% faster panning and a smoother, more intuitive map interface for built-in routable maps. Perspective view provides more detail, both close-up and further away, allowing users to better anticipate what comes next. - Garmin Epic allows athletes to combine multiple activities into one cohesive story in Garmin Connect™. Activities can be grouped together over days, weeks or months to create an "Epic", which enables users to add photos and share with family and friends, as well as see health and performance data aggregated during that period. - Enhanced rowing tools provide additional training insights like VO2 max and power curve for indoor rowing activities, while expanded rucking features let users adjust pack weight during an activity and set target metrics like calories burned. Premium design for maximum versatility Enduro 4 weighs in at an incredible 66 grams, making it one of the lightest ultraperformance smartwatches on the market. With a 51mm case, Power Sapphire™ scratch-resistant lens, titanium bezel and lightweight fiber-reinforced polymer case, it is built for the demands of the longest races and most taxing adventures, remaining remarkably light on the wrist. An integrated LED flashlight includes both white and red-light options, while a 10 ATM water resistance rating enables confident use in challenging environments. New to Enduro 4, the ComfortFit Fabric Band combines exceptional comfort, durability and moisture-wicking performance with QuickFit™ functionality, making adjustments and swapping bands even simpler. 64 GB of memory gives users more room for onboard maps, music and data, making it easier to stay prepared for extended adventures away from home. Available now, Enduro 4 has a suggested retail price of $899.99. Learn more at Garmin.com. artigo.texto: The technology industry can’t afford to ignore a growing AI data center backlash - Summary: - Concerns over environmental impact but also higher bills for their neighbors is starting to build to real social resentment Just weeks away now, the US midterms have a new factor beyond American voter cost of living or forever war concerns: whether they want what more than a few see as a potential blight on their neighbourhoods - those awful data center things. It seems a lot don't. A recent national Gallup survey reported 70% of Americans oppose data centers being built in their communities, while three-quarters of the 375 data center bills introduced in US state legislatures in 2026 seek to restrict their development in some way. Surprisingly, perhaps, it’s not just the ‘Dumocrats’ doing this: Republican candidates in states including Michigan, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania but most notably Texas, are pushing back on the President’s ‘drill, baby, drill’ pro-AI agenda. You may indeed be a 'socialist dupe’ for not loving all this new compute, but when even Erin Brockovich has set her sights on you, this is not a welcoming climate. There does seem to be a growing case file for the prosecution here: on an almost daily basis, more evidence seems to come out about the downsides of this infrastructure. Meta may be using its US data center buildout as a way to avoid paying at least £4 billion so far in Federal taxes as they are “really” R&D projects, for example, while the push for more and more data center power is driving up fossil fuel demand, nearly tripling gas-fired capacity in the United States in 2025 alone. According to at least one report, Elon Musk is even getting into the turbine-making business himself to keep up. It might not just be the environment that takes a hit from data center building frenzy; investors might soon be feeling the pain as well, given leaked Anthropic IPO plans that suggest it thinks it needs to spend a staggering $518 billion on cloud computing and infrastructure in coming years, despite possibly losing $42 billion last year - with it spending three times on infrastructure in 2025 versus 2024, $7.3 billion. Here, the AI lab’s far from being an outlier: all these guys say they want more and more data centers and more and more juice to run them. But while at least some of the public say they dislike data centers for their perceived negative impact on the water table or pumping out of carbon dioxide, it’s actually their pocketbooks that the real pushback is happening - with headlines about how Google’s proposed data center in West Memphis may ‘have’ to be paid for by a 20-year $6 utility rate hike for locals, as just one example. AI firms and some almond-based whataboutery As so often, the AI firms’ response can seem very tone deaf - like Sam Altman’s claim that 38,000 ChatGPT queries only use as much water, 0.000085 gallons, as “the production of one Californian almond;” the actual figure for the latter, say commentators, is more like 1 to 3.2 gallons, so the ratio is more like 1,000 to 11,000 queries “per almond.” Well, maybe he’s right - but the data center-AI industry isn’t being believed when it says there’s nothing to fear here. Not believed, in fact, to such an extent that, according to a September analysis by Bloomberg, local opposition “blocked or delayed” 45 U.S. data center projects worth approximately $68 billion during the second quarter of 2026. It’s not just US residents raising green fears about all this - UK citizens are also noticing, with reports of how two planned Buckinghamshire and Bedfordshire data centers potentially having higher UK carbon emissions than ExxonMobil - and with 315 more in the queue to connect to the UK’s electricity grid, the argument here, as in the US, is that fossil fuel power is the only thing available so must be used. Last month the Scottish Parliament voted to pause decisions on new AI data centers for up to a year while stricter environmental assessments and national planning guidance are developed - evidence, say activists, of a wider national UK push back against such sites. Which may or not be true, but the sector is in the spotlight. Ofgem, the national UK energy regulator, says applications in the connections queue jumped from 41 GW to 125 GW in less than a year, with data center projects accounting for at least 80 Gigawatts of that. Demand is rising so fast it’s proposing a commitment fee specifically for large data centers so speculative projects don't clog up the grid. The data center industry response So, what to make of all this? Last time we looked in depth at the “AI data centers = the burning up of Planet Earth” equation, the IT industry told us that this was a short-term problem, as renewables would end up being the main power source for all these servers and NVIDIA chips, and anyway, AI would tell us how to run these places more efficiently anyhow. Two years on and in the face of the data center backlash, what is the verdict now? The response falls into two categories: one, that the economic needs for all this are so pressing that we just need to push on, and two, well, we still need to trust that we’ll figure out how to do this more efficiently. In the words of Gary Watson, MD of Stellanor Datacenters: Some level of debate around the growth of data centers is inevitable, particularly as the scale of AI investment increases, but we shouldn’t lose sight of what these facilities actually enable; they are the backbone behind the digital services we use every day, from banking and healthcare to transport and now AI. The answer to concerns about data center growth isn’t to step back from the infrastructure needed to support the digital economy but to think carefully about where they are located and how they connect with the communities around it. artigo.texto: Hyperscale Data Held Approximately $56.4 Million of Bitcoin, Cash and Restricted Cash as of October 4, 2026 LAS VEGAS , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that, as of October 4, 2026, it held 219.9586 Bitcoin representing an aggregate value of approximately $19 million based on the Bitcoin closing price of $86,480. Additionally, the Company held approximately $37.4 million in cash and restricted cash. "We are pleased with the current financial position of the Company," stated Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data. "Our focus remains on strengthening the Company's balance sheet in order to support our core businesses and advance the development of our Michigan AI data center." For more information on Hyperscale Data and its subsidiaries, Hyperscale Data recommends that stockholders, investors and any other interested parties read Hyperscale Data's public filings and press releases available under the Investor Relations section at hyperscaledata.com or available at www.sec.gov. About Hyperscale Data, Inc. Through its wholly owned subsidiary Sentinum, Inc., Hyperscale Data owns and operates a data center at which it offers colocation and hosting services for the emerging AI ecosystems and other industries. Another of Hyperscale Data's wholly owned subsidiaries, Ault Capital Group, Inc. ("ACG"), is a hybrid private equity firm and operating company that acquires, finances, builds and actively manages businesses across financial services, digital assets, industrial services, hospitality, defense technologies and other sectors. Hyperscale Data currently expects the divestiture of ACG (the "Divestiture") to occur in 2027. Upon the occurrence of the Divestiture, the Company would be an owner and operator of data centers to support high-performance computing services, as well as a holder of the digital assets and the third wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Omnipresent Robotics, LLC. Until the Divestiture occurs, the Company will continue to provide, through ACG and its wholly and majority-owned subsidiaries and strategic investments, mission-critical products that support a diverse range of industries, including an AI software platform, equipment rental services, defense/aerospace, industrial, automotive and hotel operations. In addition, ACG is actively engaged in private credit and structured finance through Ault Lending, LLC, a licensed lending subsidiary. Hyperscale Data's headquarters are located at 11411 Southern Highlands Parkway, Suite 190, Las Vegas, NV 89141. On December 23, 2024, the Company issued one million (1,000,000) shares of a newly designated Series F Exchangeable Preferred Stock (the "Series F Preferred Stock") to all common stockholders and holders of the Series C Preferred Stock on an as-converted basis. The Divestiture will occur through the voluntary exchange of the Series F Preferred Stock for shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock of ACG (collectively, the "ACG Shares"). The Company reminds its stockholders that only those holders of the Series F Preferred Stock who agree to surrender such shares, and do not properly withdraw such surrender, in the exchange offer through which the Divestiture will occur, will be entitled to receive the ACG Shares and consequently be shareholders of ACG upon the occurrence of the Divestiture. artigo.texto: Novacium Delivers First Batch of Prototype Batteries to STAT with Twice the Energy Capacity of Batteries Currently in Service - The first batch, delivered to STAT in the third quarter of 2026, integrates GEN3 21700 cylindrical cells in place of the 18650 cells currently in service - With this first delivery, Novacium achieved two key project objectives: - Doubling the energy capacity of the batteries - Limiting geometric modifications to meet dimensional and connector requirements. MONTREAL and SOLAIZE, France, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HPQ Silicon Inc. (TSX-V: HPQ) (OTCQB: HPQFF) (FRA: O08) is pleased to inform its shareholders that its strategic partner, NOVACIUM SAS, a French deep-tech company specializing in green engineering of materials for energy applications, announces that it delivered to the French Army Technical Section ("STAT"), in the third quarter of 2026, a first batch of prototype batteries intended for tactical radio sets. Using its high-capacity cells, Novacium designed batteries offering twice the energy capacity of the batteries currently in service. This delivery follows the award, at the end of June 2026, of a contract by STAT to develop and supply, in successive batches, these high-capacity prototype batteries. Transition to 21700 Cells: Double the Capacity While Preserving Compatibility To achieve this objective, Novacium integrated GEN3 21700 cylindrical cells in place of the previously used 18650 cells. This format offers higher capacity but integrating it required preserving compatibility with existing equipment. Through an optimized cell arrangement and adapted enclosure geometry, Novacium's teams limited dimensional changes to meet STAT's dimensional and connector requirements while doubling the battery's energy capacity. A patent application has been filed for this design. Through the integration of these 21700 cells, the new battery pack reaches an onboard energy capacity of 144 Wh, twice the 72 Wh of the reference battery currently in service, and an energy density of 261 Wh/kg, compared with 160 Wh/kg for the existing solution, representing a 63% increase. An adapted battery management system (BMS), combined with this patent-pending enclosure assembly system, makes the new battery fully compatible with existing connectors, chargers, and interfaces, with only minor changes to its dimensions and mass (42.6 × 98.63 × 74.35 mm; 551 g). Under a comparable usage profile, this doubled energy capacity is intended to provide up to twice the operating time of the reference battery while retaining existing connectors and chargers. STAT will evaluate the operating time actually achieved under operational conditions. An Evaluation Campaign and User Feedback Expected in the Coming Weeks The first batch of prototype batteries delivered in the third quarter of 2026 will undergo an evaluation campaign under operational conditions conducted by STAT. At the end of this phase, detailed feedback (RETEX) will be prepared jointly by STAT and Novacium in the coming weeks. Lessons learned from this field evaluation will allow Novacium to make the necessary design, ergonomic, and parameter-setting adjustments before producing and delivering a second batch that better reflects a production configuration. "Doubling the onboard energy of a tactical radio battery while retaining the existing connectors and chargers represented an engineering challenge that our teams successfully addressed. The transition to 21700 cells enabled us to double the battery's energy capacity, and we worked to limit geometric modifications to preserve compatibility with equipment currently in service. The delivery of this first batch for evaluation under operational conditions is a key milestone: user feedback will guide the adjustments to be made before production of the second batch," said Dr. Jed Kraiem, Ph.D., Chief Operating Officer of Novacium. "The delivery of this first batch illustrates Novacium's ability to transform its anode-material expertise into batteries designed for critical applications," said Bernard Tourillon, President and CEO of HPQ Silicon Inc., which is itself President of Novacium. "If the evaluation phase confirms the expected performance, this program could provide a technical basis for offering the solution to other allied forces with comparable requirements. For HPQ, this program also illustrates the strategic value of our 36.8% interest in Novacium and of its activities in the defence sector." Next Step: A Second Batch Representative of a Production Configuration Following the evaluation campaign and RETEX, Novacium will begin production of a second batch of batteries incorporating lessons learned in the field and better representing a production configuration. This second batch will integrate Novacium's new GEN4 cells, with a capacity exceeding 6,500 mAh, with the objective of increasing the battery's energy capacity at the same mass and therefore its energy density and potential operating time. This stage aims to evaluate the solution's robustness, ergonomics, and reproducibility for potential larger-scale deployment. This first delivery forms part of the expansion of Novacium's activities in the defence and autonomous-systems sectors, notably including the order for battery packs intended for French Army drones, announced on August 19, 2026 through LN'INNOV, and the order for 100 drone battery packs from Alta Ares announced on September 17, 2026. About Novacium SAS Novacium is a French deep-tech company based in Solaize, specializing in developing and producing silicon-based anode materials for lithium-ion batteries through a proprietary process. Novacium also designs custom battery cells and packs for demanding applications, particularly in the defence, aerospace and portable-energy sectors. artigo.texto: e‑STORAGE to Supply and Commission 100 MW/200 MWh Battery Storage System for OX2 in New South Wales KITCHENER, ON , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Canadian Solar Inc. (the "Company" or "Canadian Solar") (NASDAQ: CSIQ) today announced that e‑STORAGE, its energy storage solutions business, has signed an agreement to supply and commission a 100 MW/200 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) for OX2's Muswellbrook Solar Farm and Battery, a solar-plus-storage project in New South Wales, Australia. Shipments are scheduled to begin in Q3 2027, with commercial operation targeted for Q3 2028. The battery cells and SolBank system will be produced in-house at Canadian Solar's manufacturing facilities, giving the customer end-to-end supply chain visibility and ensuring strict quality control across the product. e‑STORAGE will deliver an integrated solution built on SolBank 3.0 battery containers, paired with Power Conversion Systems (PCS), plant controls, and the Company's proprietary EQ-S Energy Management System (EMS) developed and built in-house by e‑STORAGE's North American software team. e‑STORAGE will be responsible for the R1 grid connection studies, supply the hybrid power plant controller that coordinates the battery with the co-located solar farm, and lead the overall integration and commissioning of the hybrid project. The arrangement is backed by a 20-year long-term service agreement (LTSA), placing hardware, proprietary software, and long-term performance under a single accountable partner. The project sits roughly 2.5 kilometers east of Muswellbrook, on land at a former coal mine within the Hunter-Central Coast Renewable Energy Zone. The location is significant: as the region's aging coal generators wind down toward retirement in the early 2030s, the dispatchable capacity they once provided must be replaced. Two-hour storage fills that gap directly, holding midday solar output and releasing it into the evening demand peak when supply from retiring thermal plants tightens. Once operational, the system will support the long-term hybrid power purchase agreement OX2 has signed for the project, converting variable solar output into firm, contracted supply. By storing and dispatching solar energy on demand, the BESS strengthens grid reliability in a region transitioning away from coal and helps deliver firm renewable power to the communities in the Hunter Region. Steve Symons, Vice President, OX2 Australia, said: "This battery storage system is what turns Muswellbrook into a true hybrid facility — pairing solar generation with storage so we can capture energy when the sun is shining and deliver it when the grid needs it most. It's a key step in providing firm, reliable renewable power to the Hunter region." Jeff Roy, President of e ‑ STORAGE, said: "Australia's energy transition is being decided in regions like the Hunter, where storage now has to carry the load that retiring coal once did. We control this project from the cell through to our own energy management software and 20 years of service, which means OX2 has one partner accountable for how the system performs over its full life." About Canadian Solar Inc. Canadian Solar is one of the world's largest solar technology and renewable energy companies. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Kitchener, Ontario, the Company is a leading manufacturer of solar photovoltaic modules; provider of solar energy and battery energy storage solutions; and developer, owner, and operator of utility-scale solar power and battery energy storage projects. Over the past 25 years, Canadian Solar has successfully delivered nearly 180 GW of premium-quality solar photovoltaic modules to customers across the world. Through its energy storage solutions business e-STORAGE, Canadian Solar has shipped over 23 GWh of battery energy storage solutions to global markets and had a contracted backlog of $3.5 billion as of June 30, 2026. Since entering the project development business in 2010, Canadian Solar has developed, built, and connected approximately 12.4 GWp of solar power projects and 6.4 GWh of battery energy storage projects globally. Its geographically diversified project development pipeline includes approximately 22 GWp of solar and 84 GWh of battery energy storage capacity in various stages of development. Canadian Solar is one of the most bankable companies in the solar and renewable energy industry, having been publicly listed on the NASDAQ since 2006. For additional information about the Company, follow Canadian Solar on LinkedIn or visit www.canadiansolar.com. About e-STORAGE e-STORAGE is a subsidiary of Canadian Solar and a leading company specializing in designing, manufacturing, and integrating battery energy storage systems for utility-scale applications. e-STORAGE offers proprietary battery energy storage systems (BESS) spanning battery cells, battery PACKs, power conversion systems (PCS), energy management systems (EMS) and system integration. It also provides comprehensive EPC services and full-lifecycle station operation and asset management, helping customers improve grid operations across the project lifecycle. For more info, please refer to the Media&PR section of www.csestorage.com and follow our LinkedIn page. artigo.texto: Hyperscale Data Sets November 12 as Investor Day to Discuss Michigan AI Expansion and Strategic Alternatives Across Its Portfolio Company reiterates 2027 guidance of $300–$350 million in revenue and $60–$80 million in consolidated Adjusted EBITDA LAS VEGAS , Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that it will virtually host an investor day (the "Investor Day") on November 12, 2026, from 1:15 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. Pacific Time, to discuss the Michigan AI data center campus (the "Michigan Campus"), the status of its other portfolio businesses and strategic alternatives intended to enhance stockholder value. Participation details for Investor Day will be provided at a later date. During the Investor Day, management will provide an update as to the progress on, and expansion of, the Michigan Campus and the executed master services agreement (the "MSA") with a California-based neocloud provider (the "Customer"). As previously disclosed, the MSA contemplates the deployment of an initial 20 megawatts ("MW") of critical AI compute capacity and, if the Customer exercises all of its options to extend the term, and rights to an additional 32 MW of critical AI compute capacity, the MSA could generate more than $3.0 billion in total contract revenue from the potential 52 MW deployment over a 20-year period. The Company has previously announced that it believes the Michigan Campus could ultimately support more than 300 MW of total power capacity. The development of any capacity beyond the initial 20 MW covered by the MSA is subject to financing, regulatory approvals, engineering, utility agreements, infrastructure availability, customer demand and other conditions. There can be no assurance that additional capacity will be developed, financed, contracted or placed into service. Additionally, management is expected to provide a review of the Company's various portfolio businesses within its various sectors, including: defense; energy and infrastructure; hotel operations and commercial real estate holdings; technology and finance; and commercial lending and trading and activist investing. In addition, the Company will be discussing ongoing initiatives, including, without limitation, the AI software platform by the Company's subsidiary askROI, Inc. ("askROI") and blockchain and digital technology initiatives by Ault Markets, Inc., another subsidiary. Management anticipates discussing the Company's evaluation of strategic alternatives, including potentially selling the Michigan Campus, taking public the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Sentinum, Inc. ("Sentinum") through an initial public offering or the Company's continued ownership and development of the Michigan Campus. The discussion will also address options involving askROI, including a potential sale, strategic partnership or divestiture, and the possibility of combining askROI with a broader technology business. Transactions under evaluation could include equity consideration, which would allow Hyperscale Data to retain an ownership interest in the combined business and participate in its potential upside. "We are focused on delivering the contracted capacity in our Michigan Campus and turning that investment into cash flow," said Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman. "Investor Day will also provide an update on the strategic alternatives we are evaluating for the Michigan Campus and our other portfolio businesses. Our objective is to place these businesses in structures that support their development and make their value more identifiable to our stockholders." The Company reiterates its preliminary consolidated financial guidance for the year ending December 31, 2027, of $300 million to $350 million in revenue and $60 million to $80 million in Adjusted EBITDA. Based upon known and reasonably calculated projections, including management's current operating plans, anticipated customer deployments, expected financing activities, projected digital-asset initiatives and the anticipated performance of the Company's portfolio businesses, this guidance reflects management's current projections. The Company cannot provide a quantitative reconciliation of its projected Adjusted EBITDA to the most directly comparable measure calculated under GAAP, which in this case, would be net income or loss, because certain components required to calculate net income or loss cannot presently be reasonably estimated without unreasonable effort. These components include future interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, impairment charges, acquisition-related expenses and changes in the fair value of financial instruments. These items are likely to be material to the Company's future GAAP results. No definitive decision has been made regarding any strategic alternatives under evaluation. Any discussions or considerations remain preliminary, and no assurances can be given that any definitive terms will be agreed upon or result in any transaction. Any transaction would be subject to further negotiation, due diligence, execution of definitive agreements and applicable corporate and regulatory approvals, including, as applicable, approval by the Company's Board of Directors. There can be no assurance that an agreement will be reached or that, if an agreement is reached, any transaction would ultimately be consummated. No transaction timetable is assured. "With QXDDC, our intent is for each QuantrusX™ deployment to benefit from learning across the fabric while keeping the site's data under the site's control and response decisions with the people responsible for the operation." artigo.texto: Information Services Group (ISG) Names Unisys a Leader in 2026 Private/Hybrid Cloud - Data Center Services Provider Lens® Unisys earns five Leader designations across the U.S., U.S. Public Sector and U.K. for AI-ready infrastructure, managed cloud hosting and resilient infrastructure services BLUE BELL, Pa. , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Unisys (NYSE: UIS) has been named a Leader in the 2026 ISG Provider Lens® Private/Hybrid Cloud – Data Center Services quadrant reports. These reports highlight service providers excelling in private cloud, hybrid cloud and data center infrastructure management. This marks the sixth consecutive year Unisys has been recognized as a Leader with an increase in 2026 to five Leader designations from four in 2025. ISG defines Leaders as companies with comprehensive portfolios, strong market presence, established competitive strategies and a demonstrated commitment to innovation. "Organizations are looking for infrastructure environments that can support growing AI demands while remaining secure, resilient and cost-efficient," said Chris Arrasmith, chief operating officer, Unisys. "Being recognized by ISG as a Leader for the sixth consecutive year reflects the strength of our AI-driven operations, depth of our hybrid cloud expertise and commitment to enabling clients by modernizing their infrastructure and improving their resilience, so they can operate with greater confidence and efficiency." Unisys was recognized as a Leader in five market quadrants: - U.S . AI-ready Infrastructure Managed Services for Midmarket: for connecting infrastructure transformation with ongoing operations, enabling organizations to modernize data centers and build AI-ready hybrid cloud environments. - U.S . Managed Cloud Hosting and Resilient Infrastructure Services: for delivering integrated cloud hosting, disaster recovery and infrastructure optimization services for complex enterprise environments. - U.S . artigo.texto: Commentary: Data Centers Aren’t the Only Threat to Farmland by Tim Gibbons / National Family Farm Coalition and Dena Hoff / Northern Plains Resource Council, The Daily Yonder Protests against data centers have exploded across the US, with communities revolting against a multitude of proven damaging effects on energy prices, clean air and water – and the devastation of tens of thousands of acres of agricultural land. Recent headlines in national publications report that farmers and rural communities are rejecting multimillion-dollar bids from institutional investors and tech companies to buy their farmland to build data centers. A farmer in Kentucky rejected $33 million for her farmland; another in Pennsylvania turned down a $15 million offer; and one farmer in Wisconsin even reportedly refused a whopping $70+ million bid. Land has become the next big asset class for investors, especially billionaires and private equity firms, to hide and protect their wealth. It is seen as a safe, low-risk way to park money to hedge against inflation – at the expense of farmers and local communities alike. These investors aren’t just seeking out farmland to build data centers. Just like they’re targeting housing, investment firms are buying up land and renting it back to farmers for a hefty profit. The 2024 Tenure, Ownership, and Transition of Agricultural Land (TOTAL) Survey, released this March, shows that 87% of the more than 2 million landowners renting out farmland are non-operators – that is, they are not actively farming, and the majority of these landowners never have. While these landlords raked in more than $34 billion in rent combined, the total value of farmland held for rent is $1.7 trillion – up 47% since 2014. We are watching in real time the emergence of a long-term, non-farming rural landlord class. While the TOTAL survey provides a useful indicator of farmland ownership trends, it doesn’t give us the full picture. Farmland ownership has never been effectively tracked in the US with regularity, and what limited data exists is difficult to find. The data we do have shows that investment in farmland has risen dramatically over the past two decades. Companies like AcreTrader, Farmland Partners, and others that allow individuals to invest in farmland have become increasingly popular. The most alarming growth has come from institutional investors, like pension funds, private equity firms, and wealth management groups. The value of farmland held by institutional investors has more than doubled over the past three years up to $16.6 billion dollars by 2024, an eightfold rise since 2008. Based on publicly available data alone, the largest corporate owners of US farmland control more than 2 million acres. But why are farmers selling their land in the first place? The hard truth is that farming just isn’t working as a viable livelihood anymore, and hasn’t for years. In just five years from 2017-2022, we lost 159,000 US family farms. The Farm Crisis didn’t go away in the 1980s – it’s just become quieter and less visible to most. Chronic low and volatile prices across sectors, coupled with a handful of multinational corporations tightening their iron grip over global agriculture, have pushed farmers to the brink of existence. With farm debt at an all-time high, selling the farm for the best offer possible is often the only feasible way to escape dire financial straits. And when the farm is for sale, companies with billions in assets are primed to outbid new and beginning farmers seeking land to start their own businesses. The best opportunity we have to protect farmland comes from strong federal policies that safeguard land for multiple generations of working farms and ensure farmers make a living wage. Right now, the Farmland for Farmers Act is one of the boldest pieces of federal legislation to combat this worrying trend. Modeled after anti-corporate farming laws in Midwestern states, the bill would stop large corporate entities from being able to purchase farmland only to let it lie fallow in the hopes that its value will skyrocket over time, or to rent it back to farmers at a premium price. With policies like it, coupled with a Farm Bill that allows farmers to pay their bills and sustainably grow their businesses, farmers might stand a chance. It’s long overdue for policy solutions championed by federal representatives not afraid to stand up against deep pocketed special interests. We need Congress to enact policies like the Farmland for Farmers Act that fight back against the profiteering on the backs of farmers, communities, and our natural resources. The first step in protecting farmland means supporting the next generation of farmers to enter the business with confidence and without having to compete with billionaires. We need to ensure that farmers now and in the future actually have the land they need to feed us all. Tim Gibbons is the Executive Director of the National Family Farm Coalition, a national coalition representing 30 grassroots farm, ranch, and fishing organizations in Washington, DC. A life-long Missourian, Tim has spent decades organizing family farmers, ranchers, and rural residents in support of fair, healthy and thriving rural economies, fair markets, and clean water and air. Dena Hoff represents the Northern Plains Resource Council on the NFFC Board. Since 1979, she’s raised sheep, cattle, alfalfa, corn, and edible dry beans, among other crops, on her farm in Glendive, Montana. She is an active member of and advocate for her rural community. This article first appeared on The Daily Yonder and is republished here under a Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International License.

artigo.texto: Juscelino põe postes, Fust e data centers na agenda do novo mandato Deputado e ex-ministro das Comunicações diz que pretende avançar com regras de compartilhamento de postes, recursos do Fust e infraestrutura para data centers O deputado federal Juscelino Filho, ex-ministro das Comunicações, colocou a regulamentação do compartilhamento de postes, a proteção dos recursos do Fust e a infraestrutura necessária à expansão dos data centers entre as prioridades de sua atuação no Congresso nos próximos anos. Reeleito para o quarto mandato, Juscelino afirmou na abertura da Futurecom 2026, nesta terça-feira, 6, em São Paulo, que pretende manter a agenda de telecomunicações e infraestrutura digital como uma das frentes de atuação parlamentar. O deputado preside a Frente Parlamentar de Telecomunicações e Soluções Digitais e disse que o grupo pretende atuar para dar continuidade às políticas do setor independentemente das mudanças no comando do governo federal. “É muito importante a gente ser vigilante”, afirmou ao tratar da continuidade dos investimentos. Segundo ele, a frente deverá trabalhar para garantir que políticas de Estado tenham sequência “independente de presidente que seja”. Relatório sobre postes deve ser apresentado Entre as pautas legislativas citadas está o PL 3.220/2019, que trata do compartilhamento de postes entre os setores elétrico e de telecomunicações e tem Juscelino como relator na Câmara. O deputado afirmou que ouviu empresas, entidades e especialistas dos dois setores e que pretende apresentar “em breve” seu relatório. A regulamentação dos postes é uma discussão de longa duração entre telecomunicações e distribuição de energia, envolvendo ocupação, preço, regularização das redes e responsabilidades das empresas que utilizam a infraestrutura. Fust volta ao centro da disputa orçamentária Juscelino também voltou a defender mecanismos que impeçam o contingenciamento dos recursos do Fundo de Universalização dos Serviços de Telecomunicações. Em seu discurso, lembrou que o Fust passou a financiar projetos de infraestrutura depois de mais de duas décadas de existência e citou aplicações em redes de fibra, escolas, áreas rurais e comunidades. O ex-ministro defendeu a continuidade dessa utilização e afirmou que o Congresso precisa garantir os recursos necessários aos investimentos. A questão também apareceu no quebra-queixo com Frederico. O atual ministro confirmou que existe uma discussão dentro do governo sobre restrições aos recursos e disse estar negociando com outras áreas do Executivo para preservar investimentos em infraestrutura digital. Redata é apenas uma etapa, diz Juscelino Na agenda de data centers, Juscelino afirmou que a aprovação do Redata representa um passo para atrair novos investimentos, mas relacionou o desenvolvimento desse mercado a uma infraestrutura mais ampla. Em sua intervenção, mencionou a necessidade de redes robustas, cabos submarinos, fibra óptica, energia e instrumentos de financiamento. “Não adianta você só ter o data center em algum lugar se você não tiver uma rede robusta, se você não tiver conectividade, velocidade, para esses dados estarem trafegando”, afirmou. O deputado também apontou a regulamentação do Redata como a próxima etapa e observou que, depois dela, haverá a discussão do ICMS com os governos estaduais. A avaliação converge com a posição apresentada pelo governo de São Paulo na Futurecom: o estado pretende discutir a adequação de sua tributação depois da regulamentação federal. Continuidade das políticas entra no debate A diferença entre a fala de Juscelino e as manifestações mais institucionais da abertura está na preocupação explícita com a continuidade das políticas públicas após a próxima mudança de ciclo político. O deputado defendeu que investimentos em conectividade e infraestrutura digital sejam tratados como políticas permanentes, independentemente de quem ocupe a Presidência. A agenda apresentada por Juscelino reúne, assim, questões que estão em diferentes estágios: o Redata já passou pelo Congresso e depende de regulamentação; o compartilhamento de postes continua em tramitação; e a proteção dos recursos do Fust permanece vinculada às decisões legislativas e orçamentárias. Para o setor de telecomunicações, essas três frentes deverão ocupar parte relevante da agenda do Congresso no encerramento de 2026 e no início da próxima legislatura.

artigo.texto: EcoPro BM (247540) is strengthening its strategic partnership with Samsung SDI (006400) with the aim of commercializing sulfide-based solid-state batteries in 2027. EcoPro BM said on the 6th that it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Samsung SDI to cooperate on materials development for solid-state batteries. The two companies will pursue joint research and development in solid-state batteries, a core next-generation battery technology. EcoPro BM and Samsung SDI plan to strengthen their cooperation framework from the early development stage through quality evaluation and the establishment of mass-production systems, raising both technological maturity and business competitiveness. They will also widen the scope of cooperation across core materials, including cathode materials for solid-state batteries as well as electrolytes for cathodes and for separators. Samsung SDI will work on solid-state battery cell development and the advancement of mass-production technology, while EcoPro BM will handle the development of core materials for solid-state batteries. Solid-state batteries can improve safety and performance at the same time, making them a key technology for future industries such as electric vehicles and humanoid robots. EcoPro BM has secured proprietary process technology in sulfide-based solid electrolytes, a core material for solid-state batteries, and operates a pilot plant with annual capacity of 40 tons. In August, the company was selected for the "Super Eul Project," a government program supporting materials, parts and equipment companies run by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, in recognition of those research and development results. Through the program, it will receive 20 billion won in research and development support over more than seven years. In July, EcoPro BM unveiled a full value chain roadmap for solid-state batteries at an investor briefing for retail investors. "We are currently reviewing trial production with leading customers, and we expect the earliest mass-production timing to be 2027," said Kong Bo-hyun, an executive director in charge of research and development at EcoPro BM. "We have completed the design of the mass-production line and are preparing so that construction can begin immediately in line with customer demand."

artigo.texto: Judge dismisses lawsuit challenging $2.8B Valara data center in S.C. SPARTANBURG COUNTY, S.C. (WRDW/WAGT) - A judge has thrown out a lawsuit that sought to block permits for Valara Holdings’ $2.8 billion data center in South Carolina. The group Concerned Citizens of Spartanburg County argued the county broke its own rules by approving the project as a “minor” development, which gets staff-only review with no public hearing. They said a project this big should have gone through “major” review, with public notice, public comment and a Planning Commission vote. Judge J. Derham Cole Jr. threw the case out Oct. 6 for two reasons: - No specific harm shown: The judge said concerns about noise, dust, traffic, transparency and health were too general. Under state law, neighbors must show they were “specially damaged” to block a project. - Wrong process: The judge said the group should have appealed to the county’s Board of Zoning Appeals within 10 days first, before going to court. He also said the fight over the second permit is too early because the county hasn’t decided on it yet. That second application — for four new buildings, a power yard and cooling systems, is still pending. The first permit to redevelop the old Kohler plant was approved in August 2025. The ruling also ends the group’s bid to pause construction. A judge heard that pause request Sept. 17 and took it under advisement. In August, state regulators dismissed a separate challenge over Valara’s plans for gas turbines to power the site. In June, Spartanburg County paused new data center applications for one year, but that does not stop Valara, which was already underway. Read the order in full: Copyright 2026 WRDW/WAGT. artigo.texto: Key Stats for Amazon Stock - Price change for Amazon stock in last 6 months: 18% - $AMZN Stock Price as of Oct. 2: $252 - 52-Week High: $287 - $AMZN Stock Price Target: $331 What Happened? Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) said its cloud unit will invest more than $1 billion over the next five years. The money will go to US communities that host its data centers. Amazon Web Services made the announcement on Friday. The plan covers education, job training, and energy affordability. It also covers water and energy preservation. AWS also promised to tackle the impact of its data centers on electricity and water use. The move makes sense. Data centers power and run AI models. But communities across the US have pushed back. They worry about electricity demand and utility costs. AWS noted that more than 100 data center moratoriums are being considered nationwide. The backlash is also a political issue ahead of the US midterm elections on November 3. Amazon said it invested $276 billion in data centers between 2011 and 2025. It has large projects or expansions planned in Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Virginia, and Mississippi. AWS CEO Matt Garman said the buildout is urgent. He said other countries also see the benefits of AI. He added that the countries leading in AI will shape it. AWS also said it will be water positive by 2030. That means it will return more water to communities than it uses. It says it is 75% of the way there. What the Market Is Telling Us About Amazon Stock $1 billion is small compared with what Amazon spends. On the Q2 call, management said it expects about $220 billion in cash capex this year. Most of that supports AI and AWS. So this pledge is more about public trust than cost. That trust matters for Amazon stock. AWS is the growth engine. Revenue rose 36.7% last quarter, its fastest pace in 18 quarters. Backlog reached $496 billion. AWS also posted $16.6 billion in operating income. Management says demand is higher than capacity. It expects that to stay true in 2027. New data centers are how Amazon meets that demand. If local opposition slows approvals, that could hold back growth. That is the real risk for Amazon stock. Amazon also said it plans to double its power capacity by the end of 2027 from 2025 levels. Community support will help make that possible. For now, the market will likely stay focused on AWS growth and capex returns. Still, rising local pushback is worth watching. Any new moratoriums could affect how investors view Amazon stock. A clear community plan may ease some of that worry for Amazon stockholders.

artigo.texto: Company to Highlight Passive and Semiconductor Technologies and Reference Designs for Battery Management, Protection, and Power Conversion MALVERN, Pa., Oct. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vishay Intertechnology, Inc. artigo.texto: Amazon warns $68 billion in blocked data centers threatens US AI lead — AWS CEO decries 100 proposed bans, pledges $1B community fund Various countries intentionally seeding misinformation in the U.S. about data centers to trick us into slowing down - AWS CEO Amazon has issued grave warnings to communities opposing data centers, stating that their actions could cause irreversible damage to the U.S. economy and national security. In a lengthy 3000-word post earlier today, October 2, CEO of Amazon Web Services (AWS), Matt Garman detailed the many benefits of Artificial Intelligence, comparing the technology’s impact on the economy to those of modern transportation systems and the Internet, before attempting to debunk “myths” around data centers and calling on local communities to be more receptive to build-outs as a matter of national urgency. The post also details Amazon's plans to do more for data center host communities through its “Built Together” community investment frameworks. After outlining AI’s impact and the need for data center buildouts, Garman explained why it was imperative for the U.S. to lead the AI race. “The countries that lead in AI will shape it and get the most from it in the short and long run. The choices we make today will determine that outcome, and a lapse in our nation’s focus or resolve could put us behind, and potentially irreparably so,” he wrote, presenting urgent buildouts as a key factor in leading that race. Next, Garman addressed growing anti-data center movements that have reportedly blocked data center projects worth $68 billion in the second quarter of 2026 alone, warning that if the 100 data center moratoriums being considered across the country should go through, “the US could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations.” He also pointed out that unlike transportation infrastructure, the comparably critical data center buildout is not funded by taxpayer money, but by private firms. The post dismissed many of the concerns about the buildouts as myths, then proceeded to attempt to debunk them. Garman said that, contrary to popular belief, “Data centers actually use very little water relative to other industries,” a position many hyperscalers have repeated. Amazon earlier claimed that its data centers consume only 0.075% of the water Americans use to water their lawns and gardens. Garman also claims the narrative that data centers are driving up energy bills is “misleading and convenient scapegoating.” He argues that AI is simply precipitating an expansion of power infrastructure that was always bound to happen. “Once we collectively build out this new capacity, again funded by the private sector, it should lead to flat or lower rates in the future for residents living in communities with these expanded grids,” he said. On the other hand, contradictory reports claim that AI data centers trigger a "massive irreversible" 76% electricity price spike. The U.S. House also recently passed a bill that directed regulators to consider making AI data centers pay for grid upgrades to minimize the impact on residents. The bill was eventually rejected in the Senate, with opponents saying it was "toothless" and didn't do enough to protect residents. Speaking on pollution, Garman says that data centers emitting huge amounts of pollution with their large backup diesel generators is a myth. He claims that while data centers have rarely used backup power in case of a power outage, this is only necessary because many industries depend on the facilities. This claim doesn’t exactly address growing concerns of pollution from gas turbines powering off-grid data centers. Elon Musk recently came under fire for using unlicensed gas turbines at the Colossus data center. Lastly, Garman said claims that communities do not benefit from data centers are false, citing “considerable tax revenue, positive economic impact, large numbers of good jobs, and education programs” as some of the benefits to the communities where data centers are built. Microsoft pledged to invest $1 billion in local infrastructure improvements in its Hyperion data center community and had reportedly awarded $1.6 billion in contracts to local businesses since construction began, in addition to paying teacher bonuses. As benefits specifically on Amazon’s part, Garman listed an estimated $3 billion in taxes to St. Joseph County, Indiana, over time; more than $1 billion already contributed to communities across the U.S.; thousands of jobs created in building and running the data centers; and education programs with over 10,000 educators and learners enrolled. U.S. President Donald Trump appears to agree, at least on the “revolutionary impact” aspect, and has repeatedly expressed a desire to maintain a lead over China. artigo.texto: NY Senate candidates spar over AI data centers, immigration law PLATTSBURGH, N.Y. (WCAX) - Candidates in New York’s 45th Senate District met in a debate on Tuesday, with incumbent Republican Dan Stec facing Glens Falls nurse practitioner and Democrat Melissa Seale ahead of the November election. A panel asked the candidates several questions, including their thoughts on New York’s one-year AI data center moratorium. “If there’s adequate energy there, then why shouldn’t it go forward? That should be a decision that’s made locally and not from Albany, which is why I opposed the moratorium,” Stec said. “The biggest thing is making sure these AI data centers do not impact our communities, the people and the environment,” Seale said. Both candidates also provided their views on statewide immigration policy. Debate panel member Alek LaShomb: Local Cops, Local Crimes Act passed this year that prohibits local law enforcement from working with federal immigration officials on civil investigations. Do you think this legislation goes far enough or would you like to see this peeled back a little bit? Melissa Seale: If we are having our community police officers do the work of immigration, which is a federal program, it’s taking away from our communities and I feel it could make them less safe. Dan Stec: You do not want cops knowing one thing and their brothers and sisters in law enforcement having any ability to work with each other; it’s just unsafe for everybody. Stec and Seale also said they would work to get a constitutional amendment on former state prisons to voters. That proposal would take three vacant state prisons out of the forest preserve and make them available for development. “We have a housing crisis; how can we be creative in utilizing these facilities?” Seale said. While Seale said she doesn’t know how much land should be exchanged for the trio, Stec said he would compromise on a higher amount. Alek LaShomb: If environmentalists say we want more than two thousand acres for all three back into the forest preserve, would you support that? Dan Stec: Yes, I would like to know what exactly we are talking about as far as what 2000 acres that is as I am sure they would, but there’s no magic number for me. Mountain Lake PBS’ full debate airs Friday, Oct. 9 at 8 p.m. You can also watch online and on the PBS app. Election Day is Nov. 3. Copyright 2026 WCAX. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia Os créditos de carbono classificados como de alta qualidade pela MSCI tiveram valorização de 75% em 12 meses e chegaram a US$ 14 por tonelada, enquanto os de menor qualidade são negociados abaixo de US$ 2. Os dados foram apresentados por Guy Turner, diretor-geral da área de mercados de carbono […] 7 de outubro de 2026, às 14:57 Os créditos de carbono classificados como de alta qualidade pela MSCI tiveram valorização de 75% em 12 meses e chegaram a US$ 14 por tonelada, enquanto os de menor qualidade são negociados abaixo de US$ 2. Os dados foram apresentados por Guy Turner, diretor-geral da área de mercados de carbono da companhia, durante a Climate Week NYC, realizada em Nova York em setembro de 2026, e indicam avanços em três frentes: ampliação dos sistemas regulados, diferenciação de preços por qualidade e mobilização de capital. Segundo a apresentação, foram registrados US$ 5,5 bilhões em investimentos em contratos futuros e projetos, distribuídos em mais de 200 transações, com um quarto dos recursos destinado a iniciativas de remoção de carbono. Os contratos de compra antecipada de créditos de restauração da natureza monitorados pela MSCI, com entrega prevista para 2035, alcançaram US$ 45 por tonelada, alta de 10% em relação ao primeiro semestre de 2025. Sistemas regulados ganham escala No período analisado, a União Europeia passou a incluir integralmente as emissões do transporte marítimo no comércio de emissões do bloco, o EU ETS. A Indonésia avançou em normas para dar clareza e amplitude às negociações de carbono, e o México se comprometeu a lançar um sistema nacional em 2027, com cobertura de 40% de suas emissões. Na Ásia, a Índia colocou em operação um portal para administrar registros e transações do período de conformidade de 2025 a 2027, que abrange 740 entidades e mais de 700 milhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono equivalente (CO₂e). O Vietnã contabilizou as primeiras operações de seu sistema, referentes ao ciclo 2025 a 2026, e o Japão tornou obrigatório o GX-ETS, que cobre 40% das emissões nacionais de gases de efeito estufa e reúne entre 300 e 400 empresas. Para Laura Albuquerque, co-CEO da Future Climate e membra do Comitê da Ambição Net Zero da Rede Brasileira do Pacto Global da ONU, durante cerca de duas décadas a defesa desses mercados se apoiou em estudos sobre seu potencial para reduzir o custo de cumprimento das metas climáticas. “A lógica econômica permanece: direcionar recursos para oportunidades de redução e remoção de emissões que permitam alcançar essas metas com maior eficiência. A diferença é que, hoje, a experiência acumulada oferece dados concretos para orientar decisões de política pública e investimento”, afirma. Demanda corporativa e integridade No segmento de créditos, os números da MSCI mostram atividade consistente. Cerca de 4 mil empresas definiram metas pela Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), o equivalente a 4 bilhões de toneladas de emissões, e um quarto delas assumiu compromissos de emissões líquidas zero (net zero). Em 12 meses, mil novos projetos foram registrados, outros 1.150 entraram na carteira em preparação e empresas aposentaram créditos provenientes de 2.850 projetos. A projeção da MSCI indica que as aposentadorias globais de 2026 devem ficar próximas do volume de 2025, em torno de 200 milhões de toneladas. Na leitura da co-CEO, o sinal mais relevante está na distância de valor entre projetos, que torna a avaliação de qualidade parte central da decisão de alocação de recursos para compradores e investidores. A executiva observa ainda que a convergência em torno dos Core Carbon Principles, definidos pelo Conselho de Integridade para o Mercado Voluntário de Carbono (ICVCM, na sigla em inglês), cria uma linguagem comum sobre integridade, mas exige que preços e financiamento reconheçam os custos de desenvolvimento. Capital antes da receita Para as desenvolvedoras, o cenário evidencia a necessidade de recursos antes da geração de receita. “Projetos exigem recursos para estruturação, implantação, monitoramento, ratings para a verificação ao longo de anos. A valorização dos créditos de qualidade precisa se traduzir em condições de financiamento que permitam produzir essa oferta”, diz Laura. Segundo ela, os contratos futuros podem contribuir nesse processo ao conectar a demanda dos compradores ao ciclo de investimento dos projetos. O Brasil tem diferentes vias de demanda em construção: o mercado voluntário; o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE), instituído pela Lei nº 15.042, de 11 de dezembro de 2024, com os Certificados de Redução ou Remoção Verificada de Emissões (CRVEs); os mecanismos do Artigo 6 do Acordo de Paris; o programa de combustível sustentável de aviação (SAF, na sigla em inglês) previsto na Lei nº 14.993; e o Esquema de Compensação e Redução de Carbono para a Aviação Internacional (Corsia). Na avaliação da executiva, são caminhos com regras e escalas distintas, que precisam ser considerados na estruturação dos investimentos. Laura pondera que preços, investimentos e aposentadorias não substituem a mensuração dos resultados climáticos, embora demonstrem uma base observável de atividade econômica, demanda e alocação de capital. “Para o país, a oportunidade está em usar essa experiência para desenvolver um mercado capaz de financiar projetos de qualidade, e o próximo avanço dependerá de transformar os sinais de demanda em capital disponível para quem entrega reduções e remoções verificáveis”, conclui a executiva. artigo.texto: Texas regulators have signed off on a long-debated move away from one of West Texas' thirstiest coal plants. The decision tests whether wind, solar, and battery storage can replace aging fuel-burning infrastructure without sacrificing grid reliability. It carries particular weight in a drought-prone region, where the Tolk plant has depended on the shrinking Ogallala Aquifer and where customers in Texas and New Mexico still rely on steady power. Here's what to know For Southwestern Public Service Company, the ruling means the Tolk coal plant near Lubbock can be retired and replaced with a new resource package: 1,100 megawatts of wind, 189 megawatts of solar, and 322 megawatts of battery storage, as CleanTechnica reported. Across Texas and New Mexico, the company says that combination should produce enough power for roughly 375,000 households. Texas regulators didn't rely on renewables alone. They also signed off on two gas peaker plants in Texas, but only under strict cost caps, allowing the utility to add limited gas backup instead of keeping the older coal plant in service. Josh Smith, a Sierra Club Environmental Law Program attorney who has spent years working on the Tolk plant, said the ruling shows there's "a common-sense path in Texas to transition away from expensive, dirty, thirsty coal. Texas doesn't need coal anymore, even as it prepares for increased demand, and today's decision clearly shows that." He added, "When Tolk closes, it will save abundant water in a drought-prone region, millions of ratepayer dollars, and eliminate millions of tons of harmful pollution every year, making rural West Texas a healthier place to live." The plant's retirement schedule had already been moving forward. SPS, which is owned by Xcel Energy, had previously said Tolk would close by 2032 under a 2020 Sierra Club agreement, then later proposed a December 2028 shutdown, as CleanTechnica reported. Rulings from the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission and Texas regulators set the closure for early 2029. More background Tolk's water demand is enormous. Sierra Club's analysis, Watts Wasting Texas Water, cited by CleanTechnica, said Tolk drew 1.2 billion gallons of groundwater in 2024. In 2015, its water use reached 3.3 billion gallons. Renewable energy uses very little water during operation. Closing the plant could ease pressure on the Ogallala Aquifer, a crucial groundwater source that has been under strain for years, while also reducing pollution tied to coal combustion and transport. The pollution concerns are significant as well. In 2025, Sierra Club figures cited by CleanTechnica said Tolk emitted 3.2 million tons of carbon pollution, along with 5.4 million pounds of nitrogen oxide pollution and 15.5 million pounds of sulfur dioxide. A 2026 Sierra Club health analysis linked the plant to 10 premature deaths each year, mostly in surrounding rural counties. Sierra Club said the closure should also mean fewer open-air rail shipments of coal from Wyoming, reducing coal dust and particle pollution along the route. What's being done? Texas regulators capped costs on the gas peaker plants, while the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission allowed the renewable and gas construction to move forward but, as CleanTechnica reported, didn't rule on the utility's request to classify the new gas-fired power plants as zero-carbon resources. Cyrus Reed, the Legislative and Conservation Director of the Lone Star Chapter of Sierra Club, said the approved replacement mix is the most practical option available. "These solar, wind, and battery storage projects are clearly the most cost-effective and efficient means of replacing the aging and increasingly expensive Tolk coal plant while also maintaining system reliability, saving scarce groundwater resources, utilizing existing transmission rights, and reducing harmful pollution," Reed said. Where can I learn more? These stories follow the same change for Tolk, with utilities leaning on solar and battery storage to replace older plants across the country. • Near Dallas, developers launched a major solar-and-storage buildout to help meet Texas demand. • In Texas, a massive solar farm entered service with 80 MWh of batteries. • In San Antonio, CPS Energy added a massive new battery to back up peak demand. • Duke Energy is turning a massive coal plant overhaul into solar-and-battery capacity. • In Kentucky, regulators approved an unprecedented solar expansion after retiring seven fossil plants. artigo.texto: BYD continues to develop its technological potential in the field of electric vehicles and energy storage, filing a patent for an innovative two-chamber battery case, which marks the beginning of the transition to a more efficient cooling solution. The patent reveals a serious engineering advance in addressing one of the biggest challenges facing lithium-ion batteries - managing extreme thermal loads during ultra-fast charging. The new architecture relies on dividing the battery into two isolated sections. The lower compartment is designed to be filled with a dielectric coolant, in which the battery modules themselves are directly immersed, while the upper chamber remains completely dry and contains the sensitive electrical equipment and control units. The main innovation in the design lies in the precise routing of the signal and power cables upwards through the top of the wet compartment, thus avoiding passage through the floor or side walls of the lower chamber and ensuring long-term tightness. Although standard industrial solutions usually rely on indirect plate cooling, full immersion in a dielectric liquid ensures significantly faster heat dissipation and perfect thermal uniformity between individual cells. This allows the system to maintain high charging capacities without the risk of cell degradation or activation of current-limiting protection mechanisms.

artigo.texto: MAHOMET – Mahomet officials have ended talks with a data center developer after facing backlash from the community, Village President Jason Tompkins announced Monday. Officials had been in talks with Clean Cloud Energy, a data center developer based on the east coast, about a proposal to build a data center in the village as early as January. “I have publicly opposed this project,” Trustee Bruce Colravy said in a statement. “I am proud of those in the community and surrounding area who spent time and energy standing in opposition to it. They have made a difference.” In a press release, officials said questions and concerns from residents played a “significant role” in making this decision. “Our responsibility is to carefully evaluate potential developments and determine whether there is a path forward that serves Mahomet’s interests,” Tompkins said. “Listening to our residents is an essential part of that responsibility.” The press release states officials are still committed to attracting commercial development and expanding the village’s commercial tax base, but they will focus on opportunities that align with the community’s priorities and long-term interests, which does not include data centers. Champaign County currently has a one-year pause on data center development, but it does not apply to development within Mahomet. The data center moratorium ends next spring and was put in place to allow a task force to develop new guidelines for future large-scale projects in the county. Many residents have called for the county to outright ban data centers, but some county officials say they lack the authority to do so without home rule. An effort to put home rule on the November ballot was thwarted in August by a bipartisan group of board members, saying they lacked information to make an informed decision on the issue. State lawmakers have not enacted data center regulations thus far, but Gov. JB Pritzker has called on legislators to take up the issue in the November legislative veto session. In the meantime, he paused the state’s data center tax incentive and released a framework to regulate data centers.
