artigo.texto: This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Joseph LeGare, a 24-year-old project engineer based in Frederick County, Maryland, who works at Rowan Digital Infrastructure, a hyperscale data center developer. It has been edited for length and clarity. I studied philosophy for two years at The Catholic University of America before dropping out and working as an assistant superintendent at a construction company. After about a year, I moved into residential and did administrative work, including daily reports, county inspection scheduling, quality verification, and weekly safety meetings with foremen. I even worked as a materials management specialist at a residential home manufacturer. At the same time, I was taking night classes in construction management at Frederick Community College. I assumed I'd go into residential construction, but my classes made me realize I really wanted to pursue commercial construction. I wanted to get out of office work and back into the field. My professor said that if I wanted field experience, getting into the data center industry would be a game changer. The data center industry caught my eye because it's so fast-paced Rowan Digital Infrastructure, which builds data centers, ran an internship program with my school, and one of my professors recommended I apply. They hired me full-time after six months. The data center industry uses the most up-to-date technologies to build projects — whether those technologies are related to safety equipment, heavy equipment, or tools — and it's fascinating to see. I enjoy working in the data center industry, as there is a massive need for it, and I want to help build the infrastructure that keeps the world running. As an intern, my mornings started with reviewing data center drawings I learned to read construction drawings and specifications while gaining hands-on field experience. These are data center-specific, but they share many similarities with general commercial construction drawings. The only real difference is that when we follow our drawings, we build a data center. It could just as easily be for a warehouse or apartment building. Most mornings, my mentor and I reviewed the drawings and specs. Then we'd head out with an iPad or printed drawings to watch the crews work, whether they were installing or lifting a wall. In data center construction project management, you don't need specialized skills beyond those required for any other construction project. However, data center construction is extremely fast-paced work. You'll need to adapt to constant changes, whether that's new details being released, deliveries being delayed, or a schedule being pulled in. I got to be in the field, and the pay was generous My main focus was on being in the field and learning. I was also learning how requests for information, or RFIs, work and how to move between the architects, designers, engineers, general contractors, and subcontractors. The internship pay was generous, in the high five figures. I thought I might be taking a pay cut going into commercial construction. Instead, Rowan offered me a full-time job with a six-figure salary after my internship. I'm making more than I was earning at my last job. My full-time data center role focuses on getting answers One of the biggest responsibilities after being hired was overseeing the RFI and submittal process with the general contractor. I went from observer to main point of contact. Now the GC comes to me practically daily with a problem or an RFI, and I assemble the right people to get an answer. Basically, I keep all the documentation moving. Much of my job is closing the gap between what's on the drawings and what's happening in the field. When something doesn't line up, I track down the answer. That means going back through the specs, talking to the trades, and getting questions to the design team. I'm constantly coordinating to make sure everything lines up. The specific problem is different almost every day. However, probably the most common issue is that field conditions differ from the construction documents. Sometimes the issue is easy to fix, and we can make a call right then and there. Other times, we have to reach out to the design team for guidance. We also focus heavily on testing and commissioning before turnover because everything has to work reliably. Additionally, our project is a brownfield site, which means the soil contains higher amounts of regulated materials than is typical. This is because the site used to be an aluminum smeltery, so we have to work hand in hand with the Maryland Department of the Environment to ensure we avoid adding to that regulated soil and remediate it. There are pros and cons, but overall, I'm happy working in the data center industry The biggest pro is how fast my career has advanced. The opportunities I've been given are crazy, and so is the knowledge and skill I've been able to build. I thought it would take five to 10 years to get here, but the company gave me the opportunity right off the bat. The biggest con is the stress, which I didn't fully expect. Every job has its stressors, but here you're constantly on deadlines, watching budgets because there isn't endless money for a job, and maintaining relationships. There are a lot of days I go home thinking, "Man, that was a really long day." Eventually, I'd love to be a construction manager or project manager and take on more responsibility, even with the added stress. But I'm happy where I am. As hard as the stress is, it's rewarding to look at something and know I helped build it. Do you work at a data center and want to share your story? Email this editor, Manseen Logan, at mlogan@businessinsider.com.

artigo.texto: SP vai esperar regulamento do Redata para rever ICMS de data centers Vice-governador diz que São Paulo não vai mexer no ICMS antes de seis meses, prazo no qual acredita que o decreto regulamentador das isenções federais - sem qualquer relação com os estados - sairá. O vice-governador de São Paulo, Felicio Ramuth, afirmou hoje, 6, na Futurecom 2026, que o estado só deve rever a incidência de ICMS sobre equipamentos para data center após a publicação do decreto federal que regulamentará o Redata. A seu ver, este decreto vai demorar ao menos seis meses para sair. “Não adianta a gente discutir ICMS se o Redata vai acabar com isso”, afirmou durante conversa com jornalistas na Futurecom. Vale lembrar que o Redata mexe em imposto de importação, PIS/Cofins. ICMS é imposto cobrado pelos estados, independentemente dos tributos federais. E no caso dos data centers, ele será incidente pelos próximos cinco anos, ao longo do período de transição da reforma tributária. “Então são medidas, na verdade, paliativas por certo período, porque em cinco anos a gente vai ter a reforma tributária de fato efetiva”, disse. Redata e reforma passam a conviver O regime para data centers procura reduzir custos dos novos projetos. A reforma, por sua vez, altera progressivamente a estrutura de tributação sobre consumo e investimentos. Para o ministro das Comunicações, Frederico de Siqueira Filho, o instrumento utilizado é secundário diante do efeito econômico produzido. “Se vai ser o Redata ou se vai ser reforma tributária, o importante é a gente discutir o benefício”, defendeu. Já o governo paulista enfatiza o caráter transitório de parte dos incentivos e pretende calibrar sua própria política de ICMS depois que as regras federais estiverem definidas.

artigo.texto: DeKalb County considers environmental impact study on data centers DEKALB COUNTY, Ga. - DeKalb County officials are considering a proposal to commission an independent study examining the environmental and health impacts of local data center developments. DeKalb data center proposal What we know: DeKalb County commissioners discussed a proposal Tuesday night at Dunwoody City Hall to bring in a third-party group to evaluate how large data centers impact local land, water and air. Commissioner Ted Terry introduced the measure to ensure health and environmental effects are understood before decisions are made on future developments. The board did not take a vote Tuesday, but members placed the proposal on the agenda for their next full meeting on Tuesday. Community health concerns What they're saying: Some local residents oppose hyperscale facility expansions, raising concerns over water systems, increased power demands and rising residential utility bills. Resident Gina Mangham said the issue centers on resident health, quality of life and rising noise pollution. Resident Rosalind McIntyre warned about heat islands and air pollution. Terry emphasized that he wants to limit the scale of future developments, require renewable energy, ban diesel generators and enforce buffer zones around neighborhoods. Existing development freeze The backstory: DeKalb County currently operates under a moratorium that pauses new data center applications through March. According to Terry, no applications for zoning or building data centers can be received while the moratorium remains active. DeKalb data center study What we don't know: Commissioners have not yet selected an outside firm to conduct the third-party study. It remains unknown whether the board will officially approve funding for the environmental study during their upcoming vote on Tuesday. The Source: The information in this story was gathered from a broadcast report by FOX 5 reporter Christopher King, who covered the DeKalb County Commissioners meeting in Dunwoody, as well as on-record statements from DeKalb County Commissioner Ted Terry and local residents Gina Mangham and Rosalind McIntyre.

artigo.texto: Galileo secures approval for 250 MW of battery storage in Italy Renewable energy developer Galileo has secured permits for two battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in Italy, totaling 250 MW of power capacity and 1.5 GWh of energy storage. The company expects approval for a further 100 MW of battery storage projects in the coming weeks. The approvals mark another step in Galileo’s expansion in Italy, where grid-scale battery storage is becoming increasingly important for integrating renewable energy and balancing electricity supply and demand. For Europe’s energy storage and power electronics sectors, the projects highlight growing opportunities for battery technologies, power conversion systems and grid infrastructure as Italy accelerates its energy transition. Two large-scale battery projects The newly approved developments comprise two 125 MW BESS installations, one with 1,000 MWh of storage capacity and the other with 500 MWh. The first project will be capable of delivering its rated power output for eight hours, while the second offers four hours of storage duration. Located in Italy’s North and Centre-South electricity market zones, the projects are positioned in areas where energy storage can help manage fluctuations in renewable generation and support grid stability. Both projects were originated, designed and developed by Galileo’s Italian team, which managed the entire permitting process from site identification through to authorization. According to the company, the developments incorporate advanced technology and safety standards, alongside measures to reduce environmental impact through site selection, natural screening and landscape mitigation. Local municipalities were consulted during the permitting process, with agreements reached on territorial compensation measures. More than 650 MW approved in 18 months The latest consents add to Galileo’s growing portfolio of renewable energy projects in Italy, where the company has secured approvals for more than 650 MW of solar PV and battery storage capacity over the past 18 months. Francesco Dolzani, Managing Director for Galileo in Italy, said: “Securing consent for a further 250 MW of BESS projects is another important milestone for Galileo in Italy, where in the last 18 months we have secured consents for over 650 MW of solar PV and BESS projects. We are now focusing on progressing these projects towards construction and continue working very closely with our local stakeholders.” Galileo targets independent power production Galileo’s Italian development pipeline now exceeds 3 GW, covering utility-scale solar PV, battery storage, and onshore and offshore wind projects. Across Europe, the Zurich-based company is developing approximately 17 GW of renewable energy and storage capacity. The latest approvals also support Galileo’s plans to expand its role as an independent power producer (IPP), moving projects from development toward electricity generation and storage operations. Ingmar Wilhelm, co-founder and CEO of Galileo, said: “These latest BESS consents further strengthen Galileo’s multi-technology pipeline of more than 3 GW in Italy. We will embark on our IPP trajectory in Italy, one of Europe’s most energy dependent countries, with a selection of high-quality green energy projects in the near future.”

artigo.texto: Um projeto em análise na Câmara dos Deputados pretende permitir que pequenos geradores de energia comercializem créditos de carbono correspondentes à redução de emissões obtida por suas atividades. A proposta trata da participação de empreendimentos de menor porte em operações com ativos ambientais e busca reconhecer, dentro das regras do mercado de carbono, resultados climáticos que possam ser comprovados. Na prática, a iniciativa relaciona duas atividades que normalmente são analisadas separadamente: a produção de eletricidade e a geração de benefícios ambientais mensuráveis. Caso avance, o texto poderá criar uma possibilidade adicional de remuneração para unidades que reduzam emissões em comparação com uma alternativa mais intensiva em carbono, desde que essa redução seja demonstrada pelos procedimentos exigidos. A medida ainda está em tramitação e não produz efeitos imediatos. Para que um crédito de carbono seja negociado, não basta a existência de uma instalação de geração de energia. É necessário comprovar a redução de emissões, aplicar uma metodologia reconhecida e cumprir as etapas de validação, registro e certificação previstas para esse tipo de ativo. O que a proposta pretende mudar O projeto prevê a possibilidade de que pequenos geradores tenham acesso à comercialização de créditos de carbono. A ideia é considerar a redução de emissões associada à geração de energia em menor escala como resultado passível de reconhecimento no mercado de carbono. O texto não transforma automaticamente toda unidade de pequeno porte em uma geradora de créditos. O reconhecimento dependerá da comprovação de que houve uma redução efetiva, adicional e mensurável de emissões, conforme os critérios aplicáveis ao projeto. A negociação também dependerá do atendimento às exigências previstas para o registro do ativo ambiental. Esse ponto é relevante porque créditos de carbono não correspondem simplesmente à quantidade de energia produzida. Eles estão relacionados à diferença entre as emissões que ocorreriam em determinado cenário e as emissões verificadas depois da implantação ou da operação de um projeto. A conversão dessa diferença em crédito exige regras para evitar dupla contagem e assegurar que o benefício ambiental seja atribuído a uma única iniciativa. Como funcionaria a geração do ativo ambiental Em linhas gerais, um projeto de energia precisa estabelecer uma referência para as emissões que seriam produzidas sem a atividade analisada. Em seguida, são calculadas as emissões efetivamente associadas à operação do empreendimento. A diferença entre esses dois cenários pode servir de base para a emissão de créditos, desde que o resultado atenda aos critérios técnicos e regulatórios. O processo costuma envolver a definição da metodologia, a coleta de dados, a elaboração de documentos do projeto, a avaliação por entidades habilitadas e o registro dos créditos em sistemas reconhecidos. Também é necessário acompanhar os resultados ao longo do tempo para demonstrar que a redução declarada ocorreu de fato. O projeto em análise na Câmara trata da possibilidade de participação dos pequenos geradores nesse sistema. As exigências técnicas e os mecanismos específicos para a comprovação dos resultados continuam condicionados às regras que venham a ser aplicadas ao modelo e à regulamentação correspondente. Participação de unidades de menor porte A discussão alcança geradores que, pela escala, podem enfrentar mais dificuldades para participar de operações estruturadas no mercado de carbono. Projetos menores tendem a produzir volumes individuais reduzidos de créditos. Por isso, os custos de medição, elaboração de documentos, auditoria, certificação e registro podem ter peso maior na viabilidade econômica de cada empreendimento. Ao admitir a possibilidade de comercialização por pequenos geradores, a proposta abre espaço para que esses projetos sejam considerados de forma específica nas operações com créditos de carbono. O texto, porém, não elimina a necessidade de comprovação nem estabelece que a geração de energia, isoladamente, seja suficiente para produzir um ativo negociável. A eventual participação poderá exigir a organização dos dados de diferentes unidades, a adoção de procedimentos padronizados ou a contratação de estruturas responsáveis pela gestão dos créditos. Essas condições dependem do conteúdo final da proposta e das regras que venham a disciplinar sua aplicação. Relação com o mercado de carbono O mercado de carbono reúne mecanismos pelos quais reduções ou remoções de gases de efeito estufa podem ser convertidas em unidades negociáveis. Essas unidades podem ser usadas por compradores interessados em compensar emissões, cumprir compromissos ambientais ou atender obrigações previstas em determinados sistemas regulatórios. Há diferenças entre créditos gerados por projetos e permissões de emissão vinculadas a um sistema regulado. O projeto em análise trata do reconhecimento da redução de emissões atribuída a pequenos geradores e de sua possibilidade de comercialização como crédito de carbono. A efetiva utilização desses ativos dependerá do mercado em que forem aceitos e das regras aplicáveis a cada operação. Para que o crédito tenha validade e credibilidade, o resultado ambiental precisa ser verificável. Entre os aspectos normalmente observados estão a existência do projeto, a metodologia usada para calcular a redução, a consistência dos dados, a ausência de dupla contagem e a permanência do benefício quando esse fator for relevante para a atividade. Tramitação ainda pode alterar o texto Como a proposta está em análise no Legislativo, seu conteúdo pode ser modificado durante a tramitação. O projeto ainda terá de passar pelas etapas previstas para sua apreciação, com avaliação pelos órgãos e comissões competentes, antes de eventual votação e transformação em norma. A aprovação não significaria a emissão imediata de créditos por todos os pequenos geradores. Seriam necessárias regras para definir quais projetos

artigo.texto: LG Electronics expands chiller production for AI data centers The company plans to invest a total of USD 110 million in a new air-cooled chiller production facility in the US and in expanding two air-cooled chiller production lines in South Korea. LG Electronics (LG) is expanding its chiller manufacturing capabilities with a new production facility in the United States and increased production capacity in South Korea, further strengthening its ability to deliver end-to-end cooling solutions for AI data centers (AIDCs). The company’s new air-cooled chiller production facility in Windsor, Virginia will produce air-cooled chillers for AIDCs, with production scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. The facility’s chiller production will support a stable, responsive supply system for rising demand across North America, while serving as a strategic base for LG’s regional expansion, the company said. LG is also expanding its air-cooled chiller production lines in Pyeongtaek and Changwon, South Korea. The company is improving operational efficiency by adopting a conveyor-based production system designed for mass production. The company plans to invest a total of KRW 150 billion (about USD 110 million) in its new US facility and its factories in Pyeongtaek and Changwon. LG is also broadening its AIDC thermal management business through its Chip-to-Chiller solution strategy. The portfolio includes chillers, Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs) and cold plates that absorb heat directly from chips. LG is pursuing additional AIDC projects in North America through its relationships with leading hyperscalers and big tech companies. In Asia, LG is applying its “One LG” strategy by combining heating, ventilation and air conditioning technologies with battery solutions and data center design, build and operation capabilities from other LG affiliates. LG is also applying this integrated approach to Sinar Mas Group’s hyperscale AIDC project in Jakarta, Indonesia, the company said. “We will continue to strengthen our core capabilities in AI data center cooling solutions, from differentiated product technologies to production capacity,” said James Lee, president of the LG Eco Solution Company. “With these capabilities, we will ensure a stable supply and actively address rapidly growing market demand.”

artigo.texto: Desperdício de comida agora pode gerar créditos de carbono Nova modalidade de crédito de carbono busca unir redução de emissões, combate ao desperdício de alimentos e segurança alimentar Se uma empresa quiser reduzir sua pegada de carbono, pode comprar créditos de carbono emitidos pela Verra, o maior programa de certificação de créditos de carbono do mundo. Esses créditos podem ser destinados a projetos como energia renovável ou restauração de florestas, permitindo que uma empresa reivindique os benefícios ambientais de um novo parque eólico ou de árvores plantadas em uma área que havia sido desmatada. Agora existe uma nova opção: créditos de carbono para alimentos resgatados, que ajudam a financiar organizações que coletam alimentos que seriam desperdiçados e os distribuem para pessoas necessitadas. Esses créditos emitidos pela Verra agora estão disponíveis graças à Brightly, uma startup de Boston fundada em 2023 por Andy Levitt, que anteriormente fundou e comandou a Purple Carrot, uma empresa de kits de refeições à base de plantas. A Brightly já tem contratos com mais de 25 organizações de resgate de alimentos. Agora, porém, seus créditos de carbono relacionados ao desperdício de alimentos estão sendo emitidos pela Verra, tornando-os os primeiros do tipo dentro da metodologia do padrão de certificação para reduzir a perda e o desperdício de alimentos. Os créditos de carbono são cercados de controvérsias. Pesquisas descobriram que alguns projetos não entregaram benefícios climáticos reais; especialistas afirmam que a possibilidade de usar créditos pode permitir o greenwashing. Levitt sabe que existe desconfiança em relação ao mercado de carbono, mas afirma que a solução da Brightly cria um “ciclo virtuoso de atividade” que financia ainda mais o resgate de alimentos, permitindo que organizações sem fins lucrativos alimentem mais pessoas. “Agora somos capazes de oferecer uma solução inovadora para empresas que querem se concentrar em enfrentar tanto os desafios ambientais quanto a fome”, diz Levitt. “É uma categoria e uma classe completamente novas de créditos de carbono que existem no mercado.” Reduzir o desperdício de alimentos é uma maneira clara de enfrentar as mudanças climáticas. Globalmente, o desperdício de alimentos responde por entre 6% e 10% das emissões mundiais. A aviação, para comparação, responde por cerca de 3%. Ao mesmo tempo, dezenas de milhões de americanos têm acesso limitado ou incerto a alimentos e dependem de bancos de alimentos ou despensas comunitárias para complementar suas compras. A Feeding America estima que cerca de 50 milhões de americanos receberam assistência alimentar de organizações beneficentes em 2023. Muitas dessas organizações, porém, enfrentam dificuldades de financiamento, especialmente diante do aumento da demanda provocado pela alta dos preços dos alimentos e pelo estresse econômico generalizado. ENFRENTANDO O DESAFIO AMBIENTAL E A FOME A Brightly afirma que sua solução enfrenta os dois lados dessa questão. “Nosso objetivo é criar financiamento sustentável para organizações sem fins lucrativos de resgate de alimentos, permitindo que elas mantenham os alimentos fora dos aterros sanitários e alimentem pessoas que passam fome”, diz Levitt. Ao financiar o resgate de alimentos, a Brightly afirma evitar que o metano emitido pelo desperdício de alimentos chegue à atmosfera. Uma parte fundamental de um crédito de carbono eficaz é a adicionalidade, o que significa que a redução das emissões não teria acontecido de qualquer maneira sem a receita gerada pelo crédito de carbono. A Brightly afirma quantificar os benefícios de seus créditos de carbono coletando um histórico de três anos da atividade de uma organização de resgate de alimentos, estabelecendo uma linha de base para o benefício ambiental gerado por aquela organização. A empresa contabiliza apenas o impacto ambiental que excede essa linha de base. Essas organizações sem fins lucrativos coletam todos os tipos de alimentos; algumas podem se concentrar em frutas, legumes e verduras, enquanto outras trabalham com produtos não perecíveis. Cada um desses alimentos tem seu próprio impacto ambiental. A Brightly analisa todos os dados fornecidos pelas organizações sobre o que foi resgatado e em que quantidade, atribuindo um impacto climático a cada tipo de alimento, do pão à carne. “Isso é tratado em um nível hiper específico, linha por linha, alimento por alimento, para alcançar esse grau de precisão e conservadorismo necessário para obter uma classificação de crédito de carbono de alta qualidade”, diz Levitt. Empresas que vão de fabricantes de alimentos a supermercados, e até mesmo companhias de fora do setor alimentício, como empresas de vestuário, poderiam comprar os créditos da Brightly relacionados ao desperdício de alimentos. A Brightly repassa até 80% da receita obtida com a venda dos créditos para as organizações de resgate de alimentos, financiando seus esforços e permitindo que elas ampliem suas operações. É difícil especificar quanto, em dólares, uma organização média de resgate de alimentos poderia receber, diz Levitt, porque os créditos de carbono não são criados individualmente para cada organização; em vez disso, as ações daquela organização representam uma parte de um conjunto maior de créditos. UM IMPACTO HIPERLOCAL A Brightly já analisou mais de 5 bilhões de libras de dados sobre alimentos resgatados, o equivalente a mais de 1 milhão de toneladas métricas de emissões de gases de efeito estufa evitadas. A empresa também já contratou vendas futuras de mais de 80 mil créditos. Com a notícia de que a Verra está emitindo os créditos da Brightly, Levitt espera que esse impacto cresça. A Brightly espera emitir 300 mil créditos por ano, com base em projetos de resgate de alimentos nos Estados Unidos. A empresa também está trabalhando em projetos no exterior. artigo.texto: Propostas de regulamentação sobre captura e armazenamento de carbono associados às operações de petróleo e gás. (Chinhphu.vn) - No projeto de decreto que detalha algumas disposições e medidas para organizar e orientar a implementação da Lei do Petróleo e Gás, o Ministério da Indústria e Comércio propõe regulamentações sobre as atividades de captura e armazenamento de carbono (CCS) associadas às operações de petróleo e gás. O Ministério da Indústria e Comércio declarou que as atividades de CCS associadas às operações de petróleo e gás constituem uma nova disposição em comparação com o Decreto nº 45/2023/ND-CP. As regulamentações sobre CCS no Decreto aplicam-se apenas às atividades de CCS associadas às operações de petróleo e gás no âmbito da Lei do Petróleo e Gás; a proteção ambiental, os créditos de carbono, a medição, a comunicação, a avaliação, a certificação das reduções de emissões e outras questões específicas são regidas por leis específicas relevantes. O projeto de Decreto propõe a inclusão de disposições sobre a avaliação e seleção de formações geológicas que armazenam CO₂; a implementação de atividades de CCS no âmbito dos contratos de petróleo e gás; os requisitos técnicos e de segurança para a operação de instalações de CCS; o descomissionamento de instalações de CCS; os custos recuperáveis de projetos de CCS; a receita proveniente de créditos de carbono; e os mecanismos de contabilização. Especificamente: Avaliando o potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ A minuta afirma que o relatório que avalia o potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ inclui os seguintes conteúdos principais: a) Visão geral da geologia da região, incluindo história tectônica, estrutura geológica e sistemas de falhas; b) Características geológicas e geofísicas da formação geológica que se espera armazenar CO₂; c) Resultados da simulação hidrodinâmica tridimensional do reservatório, incluindo previsões de curto e longo prazo do estado do CO₂ após a injeção; d) Calcule o potencial de armazenamento efetivo em diferentes cenários; d) Avaliar os riscos de vazamento, incluindo a análise do potencial, da probabilidade e das consequências do vazamento, e propor medidas de mitigação; e) Avaliar o impacto das operações de injeção na zona afetada pela pressão, incluindo o impacto nos reservatórios de petróleo e gás adjacentes e nas atividades de petróleo e gás existentes; g) Avaliar os riscos para as pessoas, o ambiente e os recursos relevantes, em conformidade com a lei; h) O estado dos furos de sondagem existentes que penetram a formação do reservatório e as soluções propostas para garantir a sua integridade; i) Conclusões e recomendações sobre a adequação da formação geológica para fins de armazenamento de CO₂. O relatório de avaliação do potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ é um componente do dossiê da proposta de implantação de CCS e é usado como base para o desenvolvimento do plano diretor de implantação de CCS ou do plano de implantação de CCS, conforme estipulado no Artigo 50 da Lei do Petróleo. Os resultados de levantamentos básicos de petróleo e gás, estudos gerais e estudos e avaliações de formações geológicas armazenadoras de CO₂ que tenham sido aprovados e aceitos por agências ou organizações competentes, e que atendam aos requisitos de conteúdo, qualidade e confiabilidade dos documentos, serão herdados e utilizados como base para a elaboração de relatórios sobre a avaliação de formações geológicas armazenadoras de CO₂ e planos de implementação de CCS, conforme estipulado neste Decreto. Implementação de atividades de CCS (Captura e Armazenamento de Carbono) no âmbito de contratos de petróleo e gás. De acordo com a minuta, o contratado propõe adicionar atividades de CCS ao contrato de petróleo e gás com base em um relatório que avalia o potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ e um plano para implementar atividades de CCS, conforme estipulado no Artigo 50 da Lei de Petróleo e Gás. O contratado está autorizado a receber CO₂ gerado por operações de petróleo e gás e outras atividades emissoras para processamento, transporte, injeção e armazenamento no âmbito do contrato de petróleo e gás. A captura de CO₂ em locais de emissão fora das operações de petróleo e gás deverá ser realizada em conformidade com as leis aplicáveis. A elaboração, avaliação e aprovação de alterações aos contratos de petróleo e gás, bem como a emissão de certificados de registo de investimento alterados para adicionar atividades de CCS aos contratos de petróleo e gás, serão realizadas de acordo com as disposições do artigo 18.º da Lei do Petróleo e Gás e do artigo 26.º deste Decreto. Nos casos em que as formações geológicas que armazenam CO₂ ou as zonas afetadas pela pressão se estendam para além da área do contrato de petróleo e gás existente, em blocos abertos adjacentes, a proposta, a avaliação e a aprovação para a expansão da área do contrato para fins de armazenamento de CO₂ serão realizadas de acordo com as disposições da Cláusula 4, Artigo 21 da Lei de Petróleo e Gás e do Artigo 35 deste Decreto. O plano geral de implementação de CCS e o plano de implementação de CCS podem ser incluídos no plano geral de desenvolvimento do campo de petróleo e gás, no plano de desenvolvimento do campo de petróleo e gás ou em planos de ajuste correspondentes, ou podem ser elaborados separadamente; a elaboração, avaliação e aprovação devem ser realizadas de acordo com os regulamentos pertinentes ao plano geral de desenvolvimento do campo de petróleo e gás e ao plano de desenvolvimento do campo de petróleo e gás. O plano de descomissionamento da instalação de CCS é elaborado dentro do plano de descomissionamento da instalação de petróleo e gás, de um plano de ajuste correspondente, ou é preparado separadamente e implementado de acordo com os regulamentos sobre descomissionamento de instalações de petróleo e gás. artigo.texto: By Hank Russell A Florida-based energy company has announced it is suspending operations of two of its battery energy storage systems (BESS) on eastern Long Island. NextEra Energy has agreed to suspend operations at the facility at Cove Hollow Road in East Hampton and the facility in Montauk near Fort Pond. Both facilities are jointly owned by NextEra Energy and National Grid. The suspension follows weeks of discussions between Suffolk County and NextEra. Under the arrangement, NextEra will suspend operations at both sites and remove the Novec 1230 fire suppression agent from both facilities by approximately October 9. “We are very grateful that this agreement has been reached,” said Suffolk County executive Ed Romaine. “The 2023 fire at the East Hampton BESS location, and the consequent contamination of the site and surrounding areas, prove that the operations must cease until changes are made that will protect our drinking water.” The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation has determined that, when water was applied to the East Hampton facility during a May 2023 fire, it mixed with Novec™ 1230 — a chemical agent used for fire suppression — and broke down into PFPrA, a short-chain “forever chemical,” which has since been detected in drinking water in the surrounding area. Two Suffolk County Water Authority (SCWA) wells have been taken offline. The county has drilled monitoring wells to investigate the contamination and supports the SCWA’s litigation against NextEra. In July, Romaine and East Hampton Village Mayor Jerry Larsen sent letters to the chief executives of NextEra Energy and National Grid urging them to suspend operations at the East Hampton facility until the investigation is completed. “We need a remediation plan immediately, one approved by the DEC, so the hard work of cleaning the site can begin,” said Romaine. “The community did not know for years that the 2023 fire had left behind PFPrA. They should not wait any longer for the situation to be addressed.” The county will continue its groundwater testing in the area. Long Island Life & Politics reached out to NextEra and National Grid for comment. NextEra issued the following statement: “We are temporarily ceasing operations at our East Hampton and Montauk battery facilities. We remain committed to working with local and state officials.” National Grid did not respond as of press time.

artigo.texto: Jupiter Wagons Secures 41 MW/102.5 MWh BESS Project from UPCL JEM Energy, in partnership with Madhav Infra Projects, emerged as the L1 bidder for UPCL’s Cluster C tender under the TBCB mechanism. October 06, 2026. By News Bureau Jupiter Wagons (JWL), through its energy business JEM Energy, has won a 41 MW/102.5 MWh standalone Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project from Uttarakhand Power Corporation (UPCL), in partnership with Madhav Infra Projects. The partnership emerged as the L1 bidder for Cluster C of UPCL's tender, which was conducted under the Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism. The projects envisage supply and commissioning of approximately INR 100 crore of BESS system. JWL has also received the formal Letter of Award (LoA) from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company (WBSEDCL) for the 50 MW/200 MWh standalone BESS project at the Jeerat 132 kV substation in North 24 Parganas, West Bengal. The project was secured in August 2026. These developments follow the Union Cabinet's approval of Green Energy Corridor Phase-3, which was welcomed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The scheme provides for 50 GWh of battery energy storage alongside stronger intra-state transmission networks. Substation-level storage of the kind being deployed in Uttarakhand and West Bengal is central to this framework, and JEM Energy is building its utility-scale portfolio in line with it. Speaking on the development, Vivek Lohia, Managing Director, Jupiter Wagons, said, "Winning the Uttarakhand project and receiving the formal award for Jeerat are important steps in building JEM Energy into a scalable energy storage business. With the approval of Green Energy Corridor Phase-3, battery storage is now firmly part of how India will plan and strengthen its grid, and substation-level projects such as these are where that work begins. We reiterate our target of building a BESS order book of approximately INR 1,000 crore by FY27. As the business scales, we expect Jupiter Electric Mobility (JEM) to turn EBITDA positive in Q3 FY27 and to turn profitable by FY28. artigo.texto: Raleigh leaders could decide Tuesday night whether to pause future data center development in the city. A public hearing will be held Tuesday at 7 p.m. during the Raleigh City Council meeting. Citizens will have a chance to share their opinions on whether the city should approve a six-month pause on data centers before a possible vote. Other WRAL Top Stories A moratorium is a pause, not a ban, on data centers. The conversation started months ago when the city of Raleigh received an application for a large data center on Jones Sausage Road. Raleigh is currently the largest city in North Carolina without a moratorium on data centers. Several cities and counties, including Apex, Durham, Greensboro and Charlotte, have approved similar pauses on data center development. Raleigh already has smaller data centers, but the proposed moratorium would be for large-scale data centers that raise concerns about noise, energy and water use. Raleigh Mayor Janet Cowell previously said the city has to protect its residents while maintaining its status as an innovative city. "We definitely want to protect those that are already operating and not disrupt existing research and development or companies that have located here," Cowell said. "Then we want to have a very rational and careful approach that protects individuals who live in Raleigh and still be known as a tech, innovative city." At last month's Raleigh City Council meeting, some people expressed their support for a moratorium. “When new technology develops, policy usually lags behind, and a moratorium gives you a chance to put a pause on that [and] figure out how to handle this thing," said Laura Harris, a Raleigh resident. Data centers, which support AI computing, are packed with graphics processing units, or GPUs, that generate significantly more heat than traditional computing equipment and often require large amounts of water to cool.

artigo.texto: LEXINGTON, Ky. — The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council voted unanimously to extend a moratorium on new data center development until Oct. 2027 after hearing three hours of public comment from residents and business representatives. Critics raised concerns about the potential impact of a massive data center on the environment, electric bills and quality of life. Several residents urged stronger limits, while representatives of businesses asked for more time to avoid unintended consequences from a proposed zoning ordinance. The council also changed the language of the proposed ordinance to limit smaller data centers to industrial zones. The proposal would keep a ban on data centers larger than 50,000 square feet, set a noise limit of 30 decibels and cap energy use at 25 megawatts, which is lower than the 50 megawatts sought by some developers for a local project. Council members also voted to ask the planning commission to create a new, separate zoning classification for minor data centers. In city terms, it would be an “exclusive use zone,” a designation currently used only for landfills. Some concerns focused on banking and healthcare, which rely on onsite data infrastructure such as server rooms or smaller data centers for day-to-day operations. “I believe we need a more intentional, responsible and equitable approach to data center regulations, one that clearly distinguished between principal uses and legitimate accessory uses, and strongly regulates both,” Councilmember Tyler Morton, Dist. 1 said. Morton and Dist. 4 Councilmember Emma Curtis led the motion that changed the city’s approach to regulating the rapidly evolving technology. “This is an emerging technology. Everything is changing so quickly that as soon as we think we have the right policy in place, something else changes,” State Rep. Anne Gay Donworth, D-Lexington, said during the meeting. Donworth said she has heard of colleagues in Frankfort who plan to propose new state regulations on data centers. Those bills could be discussed as early as January. Lexington’s Urban County Council is expected to discuss the issue again during its next regular meeting. It’s not clear when the local planning commission could take up the issue once again.

artigo.texto: Physical artificial intelligence company iiLab (307180.KQ) has developed a technology that can raise the energy density of small solid-state batteries by up to 10 times compared with existing products. The company removed the substrate that had taken up unnecessary space inside the battery and applied its own interface control technology, improving both energy storage capacity and high-rate discharge performance. Based on the technology, iiLab plans to accelerate its efforts to secure the core energy technology needed for humanoid robots. iiLab said on the 8th that it has developed a technology that completely eliminates the substrate, which accounted for more than 95% of the total volume in conventional thin-film solid-state batteries. Existing products are built on a silicon or glass substrate about 500 micrometers thick. Because the substrate takes up considerable space without contributing to energy storage, it has limited efforts to raise energy density. Instead of using a substrate, iiLab applied a hybrid structure combining thin and thick films to expand the space available for energy storage. Based on the active material in a coin cell the company actually produced, the energy density was calculated at 500 to 750 Wh/L, up to 10 times higher than the 50 to 80 Wh/L of conventional thin-film solid-state batteries. The company also improved high-rate discharge performance by combining the high-output characteristics of thin films with the high-capacity characteristics of thick-film electrodes and precisely controlling the interface between the two structures. iiLab plans to link the technology to its humanoid robot business. Humanoids must fit batteries into limited internal space while stably supplying the power needed for joints and drive units. That requires batteries with both high energy density and high output. The company's strategy is to internalize the core technologies of its physical AI business by adding battery technology to the robot operating data and AI technology it already has. "The key to this technology is that it solves the structural problem that had constrained the energy density of existing thin-film solid-state batteries, while improving both high capacity and high output at the same time," said Ko Jae-hwan, head of iiLab's battery R&D center. "We will continue to advance the performance and technological competitiveness of next-generation small solid-state batteries." He added, "As a company operating a physical AI operating data platform in South Korea, iiLab will strengthen the technological competitiveness of the physical AI industry by organically connecting robot operating data, artificial intelligence and core energy technology."

artigo.texto: Solid-state batteries have long been heralded as the next great leap in energy storage, promising to replace the flammable liquid electrolytes inside today’s lithium-ion cells with solid materials that could make devices safer and more energy dense. Yet a persistent engineering problem has slowed their progress: the solid materials that shuttle lithium ions between electrodes are often stiff and unforgiving, struggling to maintain the intimate contact with electrode surfaces that a working battery demands. Now, researchers at Rice University have taken an unusually elegant approach to that problem by asking a question that most electrolyte designers have overlooked — what if the material that carries the ions could also bend, flex, and adapt mechanically to the environment inside a cell? The Rice team, drawn from the departments of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Chemistry, and Materials Science and Nanoengineering, along with the Rice Advanced Materials Institute, has developed a relatively soft and flexible porous material that selectively transports lithium ions. The work, published in the peer-reviewed journal Chemical Science, introduces a new design philosophy for porous solid electrolytes, one that treats mechanical adaptability not as an afterthought but as a core performance criterion, sitting alongside ionic conductivity and chemical stability in the designer’s toolkit. The material at the heart of the study is called ZnBTCA, and it belongs to a family of compounds known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs. These are porous crystalline materials built from metal atoms connected by organic molecules into repeating, lattice-like structures. What makes MOFs so compelling for battery applications is their architecture: they contain tiny, ordered channels whose size and chemistry can be tailored to move or hold specific molecules and ions. In principle, a MOF can act as a molecular sieve for charge, allowing lithium ions to stream through its pores while blocking everything else. Many MOFs previously explored as battery electrolytes, however, have been constructed from relatively rigid aromatic linkers — the organic struts that connect the metal nodes — which produce frameworks that are stiff and mechanically unyielding. ZnBTCA takes a fundamentally different route. Instead of an aromatic linker, it employs a flexible aliphatic linker, an organic molecule with a pliable carbon-chain backbone. That single design choice ripples through the entire material: the framework itself becomes softer and more mechanically adaptable, capable of deforming and conforming rather than resisting. The researchers also emphasized practicality in their selection of building blocks. The material is assembled from relatively abundant, low-cost components, including zinc — one of the most accessible metals in the battery chemist’s repertoire — and an inexpensive aliphatic linker, an important consideration if such materials are ever to move from the laboratory bench toward real-world manufacturing. First author Zina Deriche, a graduate student in chemical and biomolecular engineering at Rice, framed the shift in thinking that underpins the work. MOF electrolytes, she noted, are often designed primarily around how effectively they transport ions. The Rice study demonstrates that the mechanical properties of the framework can also be an important part of the design equation. It is a deceptively simple reframing, but one with significant consequences: a material that can flex with the battery as it charges and discharges may hold up better over thousands of cycles than one that cracks or delaminates under mechanical stress. The dual functionality of ZnBTCA is what excites the team most. The material’s flexible molecular building blocks make it relatively soft, while its negatively charged framework structure favors the movement of positively charged lithium ions through its channels. Stavroula Alina Kampouri, a corresponding author of the study and assistant professor across chemical and biomolecular engineering, chemistry, and materials science and nanoengineering, described the convergence of these properties as the most thrilling aspect of the result. The same material, she explained, brings together flexible building blocks that make the framework softer and more adaptable with a negatively charged structure that promotes selective lithium-ion transport. Bringing those properties together, she said, offers a new way to design MOF electrolytes by considering how ions move and how the material behaves mechanically at the same time. The experimental results lend strong support to the design concept. The researchers first exchanged the sodium ions residing within the framework for lithium ions, a process known as ion exchange that is common in MOF chemistry. After the exchange, they found that roughly 95 percent of the mobile charge-balancing ions in the material were lithium, while the framework itself remained structurally intact — a critical demonstration that the delicate crystalline lattice could survive the swapping of its guest ions without collapsing. Selectivity matters enormously in an electrolyte: a material that carries only lithium ions, rather than a mixed crowd of mobile species, delivers cleaner, more efficient battery operation and helps prevent parasitic reactions that degrade performance over time. Further electrochemical testing quantified just how selective the material is. In measurements of the current flowing through the material, lithium ions accounted for approximately 79 percent of the total ionic current — a high lithium-ion transference number that indicates the framework’s channels and charged surfaces are indeed preferentially shepherding lithium rather than the counterions left behind by the exchange process. artigo.texto: O governo de São Paulo pretende discutir uma eventual redução do ICMS sobre equipamentos para data centers somente depois da regulamentação federal do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata). A posição foi apresentada pelo vice-governador Felício Ramuth na terça-feira (6), durante o Futurecom 2026, em São Paulo. Questionado sobre os percentuais de redução reivindicados pelo setor, ele afirmou que essa definição dependerá do conhecimento das regras federais. Não foi anunciado um percentual de benefício nem uma data para sua aplicação. São Paulo defende incentivo para equipamentos específicos Ramuth indicou que o estado pretende concentrar os incentivos em equipamentos de alta tecnologia destinados à inteligência artificial, como processadores e computadores de alta capacidade sem similares nacionais. A posição não contempla, da mesma forma, itens de uso mais amplo, como aparelhos de ar-condicionado. O vice-governador também afirmou que a proposta discutida entre os estados passou por alterações e se afastou do formato inicialmente defendido por São Paulo. União e estado têm expectativas diferentes sobre o prazo Ramuth estimou que a regulamentação do Redata poderia levar pelo menos seis meses. O ministro das Comunicações, Frederico de Siqueira Filho, apresentou uma expectativa mais curta: concluir o processo até o fim de 2026. Também presente no Futurecom, o ministro afirmou que a aprovação pelo Congresso superou a etapa mais difícil. Segundo ele, os ajustes restantes envolvem principalmente a questão energética e estão em discussão com outras áreas do governo. Os prazos mencionados pelas autoridades são estimativas. Não representam uma data formalmente estabelecida para a publicação da regulamentação ou para a concessão de um incentivo estadual. Redata não reduz automaticamente o ICMS O Redata foi instituído pela Lei nº 15.504, de 15 de setembro de 2026. O regime prevê suspensão de tributos federais sobre determinados equipamentos destinados ao ativo imobilizado de empresas habilitadas, com conversão em alíquota zero conforme as condições legais. A legislação contempla PIS/Pasep, Cofins, suas modalidades incidentes na importação, IPI e Imposto de Importação. Para este último, exige produtos sem produção nacional equivalente, relacionados em ato do Executivo. O ICMS não integra essa lista. Assim, a regulamentação federal não concede, por si só, redução do imposto estadual. A concessão de benefícios de ICMS segue regras próprias. A Lei Complementar nº 24/1975 prevê convênios celebrados e ratificados pelos estados e pelo Distrito Federal e exige decisão unânime dos estados representados para conceder benefícios. Por isso, a posição paulista faz parte de uma discussão que também depende da coordenação entre as unidades da Federação no Conselho Nacional de Política Fazendária (Confaz). Regulamentação terá de detalhar habilitação e contrapartidas A lei atribui ao Executivo federal a definição das condições de habilitação e coabilitação, concedidas pela Receita Federal. Também prevê compromissos relacionados à sustentabilidade, à oferta de capacidade ao mercado brasileiro e a investimentos em pesquisa e desenvolvimento. Há ainda um limite relevante para o calendário: os benefícios relativos a PIS/Pasep, Cofins e IPI têm efeitos previstos até 31 de dezembro de 2026, observadas as regras da Reforma Tributária. Para empresas e profissionais contábeis envolvidos em projetos de data centers, o acompanhamento deve considerar separadamente as condições federais do Redata e os eventuais atos sobre ICMS. Uma redução ainda em discussão não deve ser incorporada como economia garantida ao orçamento de aquisição dos equipamentos. Leia mais: Redata é sancionado e cria incentivos fiscais para instalação e ampliação de data centers no Brasil. artigo.texto: Principais Conclusões - As ações da Microsoft ganharam 37,5% no terceiro trimestre, e Jim Cramer diz que a empresa está "começando a recuperar seu investimento monstruoso em data centers". - O retorno está aparecendo na receita da Microsoft, mas seu fluxo de caixa livre caiu por dois anos consecutivos, então a recuperação está apenas começando. - Os gastos de capital da Microsoft subiram de US$ 23,9 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2022 para US$ 116 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2026, e 30 milhões de usuários do Copilot não podem cobrir essa conta sozinhos. - O ponto a ser observado é se os gastos atingem o pico enquanto a receita continua subindo em direção aos US$ 467 bilhões que os analistas esperam para o ano fiscal de 2028. No episódio de quarta-feira à noite do Mad Money, Jim Cramer, da CNBC, revisou tudo o que preocupava os investidores em junho, no início do que tem sido uma corrida incrível para a Microsoft (MSFT). Desaceleração do Azure. Muito envolvimento com a OpenAI. Clientes que supostamente não pagariam pelo Copilot. "Todas essas preocupações acabaram sendo ou erradas ou falsas", disse ele. Mas Cramer guardou o que chamou de "a maior mudança" para o final: "A Microsoft está começando a recuperar seu investimento monstruoso em data centers." Se ele estiver certo, isso muda tudo. Quão monstruoso estamos falando? O CapEx da Microsoft quase quintuplicou em quatro anos, de US$ 23,9 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2022 para US$ 116 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2026, o ano até junho… Só esse último ano foi um aumento em relação aos US$ 64,6 bilhões do ano anterior. Se é que dá para dizer, eu diria que "monstruoso" é pouco. (Claro, se você quiser se aprofundar... como meu colega explicou na terça-feira, há uma manobra contábil por trás de como os números de capex da Microsoft são relatados, o que vale a pena ler.) O argumento de Cramer para o retorno começa com o Copilot, que tem "30 milhões de usuários e crescendo. Eles estão pagando." A Microsoft claramente quer muito mais usuários do Copilot também. Na sexta-feira passada, o CEO Satya Nadella anunciou "nossa maior atualização do Copilot até hoje", apresentando-o como "um novo sistema operacional para o trabalho que abrange todos os modelos, todos os fatores de forma e todas as tarefas". O que soa bem, mas obviamente não é suficiente para justificar os gastos com capex. Pelo menos ainda não. A receita está aparecendo Mas, ao ampliar o foco do Copilot para toda a empresa, o retorno fica muito mais fácil de ver… A receita cresceu de US$ 245 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2024 para US$ 332 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2026, e os cerca de 50 analistas que cobrem a ação esperam US$ 391 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2027 e US$ 467 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2028. Esse é um crescimento sólido, mas, mais importante, desafia uma lei da gravidade: empresas desse tamanho não deveriam acelerar, mas é exatamente isso que o Wall Street espera que a Microsoft faça. Com a receita da Microsoft Cloud subindo 27% ano a ano no último trimestre (e o Azure subindo 43% – e ultrapassando US$ 100 bilhões pela primeira vez!) – há todos os motivos para pensar que tal aceleração é possível. E só é possível graças à expansão dos data centers. Agora, Cramer está um pouco mais confiante do que eu. Ele acha que os gastos com data centers "podem estar até mesmo atingindo o pico e a lucratividade está à vista", e que Nadella e a CFO Amy Hood sabiam que "esses data centers durarão muito mais tempo do que as pessoas pensavam". Se o capex se estabilizar enquanto a receita se capitaliza na taxa que os analistas esperam, o fluxo de caixa livre finalmente deve começar a subir. Essa é a aposta que os investidores fizeram neste trimestre. Então, sim, o investimento monstruoso da Microsoft está começando a dar retorno, pelo menos na linha de cima. Claro, nada nesses gráficos mostra o capex atingindo o pico ainda, e os US$ 116 bilhões do ano fiscal de 2026 são a maior conta até agora. Então, qual é o valor real da ação da Microsoft? artigo.texto: The global building boom of power-hungry data centers is straining electrical grids, causing greater reliance on energy from polluting fossil fuels. Christina Delimitrou, a newly tenured associate professor at MIT, is fighting this environmental threat by rethinking how the computer servers and networking equipment inside those data centers operate. She and her group apply machine learning to make large-scale data centers more efficient, secure, and reliable. They redesign outdated cloud computing systems, develop methods to manage shared hardware resources, and create streamlined server architectures. These advances allow data center operators to coax more computational power out of existing hardware. “If data centers are not utilized to the best of their capabilities, then they will burn much more power than they need to meet growing user demand,” says Delimitrou, the KDD Career Development Associate Professor in Communications and Technology in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) and a member of the Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL). “There is a lot of bloating, especially on the software side of these systems. If we can remove that bloating in a way that doesn’t compromise performance, then we won’t need to build as many new data centers.” She also harnesses AI to help programmers find and fix problems in cloud-based applications, like music-streaming services or video conferencing systems. This eliminates application downtime that hampers performance and drains computational resources. “By managing resources more effectively in the cloud, the end user gets more predictable performance from the application running on their smartphone,” she adds. Mathematical beginnings Delimitrou grew up in a midsized town within the vast plains of northern Greece. Her early interest in math and science was sparked, in part, by the ancient history of her homeland, where Euclid and Pythagoras studied mathematical problems more than 2,000 years ago. “In Greece, there is a long tradition of geometry,” she says. She also drew scientific inspiration from her parents. Her mother worked as a chemical engineer and her father as a pharmacist — and both encouraged their daughter’s innate curiosity. Her early affinity for math led Delimitrou to study computer engineering at the National Technical University of Athens, even though she didn’t know much about the field. She quickly gravitated toward courses that focused on the applied science of engineering. For her diploma thesis — a project all students complete during their fifth and final year of study — she studied resource management in a computer when multiple applications are running at once. “A lot of the challenges I was looking at then would get much harder if, instead of a single system, you had 100,000 of these systems. That was a problem that piqued my interest,” she says. Seeking to make a bigger impact as a researcher, Delimitrou pursued a graduate degree at Stanford University. She began tackling inefficiencies in cloud computing systems and large-scale data centers, which was a rapidly growing area of research. Through that work, Delimitrou and her research mentor, Christos Kozyrakis, the Leonard Bosack and Sandy K. Lerner Professor of Engineering, realized many large computing systems were underutilized. “You would expect, with all the demand for these systems, that they should be running close to 100 percent capacity. But we found that most were running at only about 15 percent capacity,” she says. “This is not a resource-efficient or sustainable way of scaling these systems.” Applying AI To push that utilization closer to 100 percent, she began investigating machine-learning solutions to streamline cumbersome computational processes. Machine learning could automate resource management operations in the cloud, identifying solutions that developers might miss on their own. “Applying machine learning to solve a large-scale system problem was a novel approach at the time. It was a bit risky because people had not yet shown that these techniques would work,” Delimitrou says. “But empirical approaches require a lot of expertise, and the scale of the system is so large that it is difficult for users to manage. This is why machine learning is often the best solution.” After earning her PhD, Delimitrou continued this line of work as an assistant professor at Cornell University. One tool her group developed, Seer, uses deep learning to anticipate and prevent problems in web applications before they happen. This averts widespread slowdowns that may occur if a developer tries to fix a problem manually. As she delved deeper into cloud computing, Delimitrou observed that cloud applications were changing. Developers were now splitting applications into smaller pieces to spread across multiple servers, which increases the speed of deployment. “But the servers were not built for this new style of application design. So, I rethought some of my earlier work to build machine-learning systems for this new class of applications,” she says. To tackle these new challenges, she found herself collaborating more often with faculty members who had different software and hardware expertise. Those collaborations opened exciting new research areas. A few years later, she decided to join MIT because of the opportunity to collaborate with researchers at the top of their fields in hardware and software engineering. She became an assistant professor in EECS in 2022. Creative approaches At MIT, Delimitrou also enjoys the teaching aspect of her role. One of her favorite courses to teach is 6.191 (Computation Structure), a popular undergraduate class with about 350 students each semester. artigo.texto: As ações da LG Electronics registravam forte valorização no pregão desta terça-feira (6) após a companhia fechar um novo contrato plurianual para o fornecimento de sistemas de resfriamento de grande porte (chillers) a data centers focados em inteligência artificial (IA) nos Estados Unidos. A operação reforça o reposicionamento da sul-coreana de eletrônicos de consumo no mercado B2B de gestão térmica para infraestrutura crítica de dados. A subsidiária da empresa nos EUA firmou um acordo de longo prazo com a AIR Control Concepts, plataforma de data centers sediada na Virgínia. A parceria prevê o fornecimento de soluções de refrigeração para instalações que somam mais de 5 gigawatts de capacidade computacional. Embora os valores financeiros não tenham sido revelados, a LG destacou que o contrato consolida sua entrada na cadeia de suprimentos de infraestrutura essencial para IA na América do Norte. A reação dos investidores foi imediata. Na Bolsa de Seul, os papéis da LG Electronics chegaram a subir 8,8% no início da sessão, registrando a maior alta diária em cerca de dois meses. A valorização reflete o otimismo com a diversificação de receitas da companhia para além de eletrodomésticos e telas, aproveitando o boom global de demanda por capacidade de processamento intensivo. Para dar conta do volume de pedidos, a LG anunciou planos de expansão capacidade fabril nos Estados Unidos e na Coreia do Sul. A empresa construirá uma nova planta industrial na Virgínia focada no atendimento ao mercado norte-americano, com início de operações previsto para o primeiro semestre de 2027. Em paralelo, a produção será ampliada nas unidades sul-coreanas de Changwon e Pyeongtaek. Além dos contratos norte-americanos, a divisão HVAC (aquecimento, ventilação e ar-condicionado) da empresa vem conquistando espaço em projetos de infraestrutura corporativa no Oriente Médio e na Indonésia. A LG projeta que as novas encomendas anuais de resfriamento para data centers alcancem múltiplos bilhões de dólares até o encerramento de 2026, impulsionadas pelos US$ 426 milhões já garantidos no primeiro semestre do ano. Com o ritmo acelerado de fechamento de negócios, a gestão da companhia afirmou que deve superar antecipadamente a meta estipulada para 2027, que previa R$ US$ 680 milhões em faturamento anual exclusivo na unidade de chillers.

artigo.texto: To get the carbon market off the ground:完善法律框架，政经济力材材质 ... During the 2026-2027 period, Vietnam will focus on building a foundation in terms of institutions, data, technical standards, and a blue classification system; promoting investment opportunities and developing an efficient carbon market. Vietnam is gradually laying the groundwork for a truly functioning carbon market, while simultaneously transforming climate change response goals into drivers for green transition and sustainable development. Notably, to lay the groundwork for the carbon market to "take off," the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment recently issued Decision No. 3696/QD-BNNMT implementing Decision No. 505/QD-TTg of the Prime Minister on the National Digital Transformation Day 2026; which stipulates the completion of the construction and operation of the National Registration System for Greenhouse Gas Emission Quotas and Carbon Credits before October 10, 2026. Building a solidlegal foundation According to Mr. Nguyen Hung Minh, Deputy Head of the Carbon Market Department, Climate Change Agency, greenhouse gases and the greenhouse effect are the core causes of global warming and lead to many consequences of climate change such as rising sea levels and extreme weather events. In Vietnam, the average annual temperature across the country between 1961 and 2023 has been recorded as increasing by approximately 0.2 degrees Celsius per decade. Notably, Vietnam ranks 10th in the world in terms of climate change risk in 2024. Faced with these challenges, Vietnam's system of policies and laws on climate change response has been gradually improved over time, from guidelines, laws, decrees, decisions, and circulars to international agreements and treaties. Among these, Resolution 24-NQ/TW dated June 3, 2013, on proactively responding to climate change, strengthening resource management and environmental protection; Resolution 120/NQ-CP of 2017 on sustainable development of the Mekong Delta adapting to climate change; and Government Resolution 06/NQ-CP promulgating the Action Program to continue implementing Resolution 24-NQ/TW, are fundamental policy decisions. By 2026, the focus will continue to be on building databases, early warning systems for natural disasters, developing a circular economy , efficient resource utilization, and a carbon market. However, climate change provisions are currently regulated in different laws. In particular, the 2020 Environmental Protection Law is a crucial legal foundation for responding to climate change. Specifically, Article 139 of the 2020 Environmental Protection Law provides the legal basis for organizing and developing a carbon market. This forms the fundamental basis for building a carbon market in Vietnam. Looking ahead, Mr. Minh stated that Vietnam will continue to improve its climate change legislation, including researching and proposing the development of a Climate Change Law; reviewing relevant regulations in the 2020 Environmental Protection Law; perfecting technical standards and regulations; promoting the circular economy and green transition; and strengthening the dissemination and popularization of the law. You may also like Regarding the institutionalization of the Party's major policies, the Director of the Climate Change Department, Nguyen Tuan Quang, stated that the department has spearheaded the development of a project on the management and use of carbon credits, which served as the basis for the Party Central Committee's issuance of Conclusion No. 71-KL/TW on the management and use of carbon credits to serve sustainable socio-economic development and ensure national security; and collaborated with the Department of Environment to advise on the development of Conclusion No. 75-KL/TW of the Party Central Committee on environmental protection and proactive response to climate change in the new era. The Climate Change Department has also coordinated with the Environment Department to finalize the draft Law amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Law on Environmental Protection for the Government to report to the Standing Committee of the National Assembly . It is currently undergoing further technical review to be ready for submission to the National Assembly for consideration and approval at the October session. Furthermore, the Climate Change Department has advised the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment to submit to the Government a Resolution approving the Agreement on implementation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement between Vietnam and the Government of Singapore. Currently, the Government has approved bilateral carbon credit exchange agreements with Singapore and Japan; regarding South Korea and Switzerland , the department is promoting technical negotiations, with the signing expected to be completed by the end of 2026. Dr. Tang The Cuong, Director of the Department of Environment, believes that environmental protection is no longer a preventative task, but has become the foundation of national development; it not only contributes to improving the quality of life for people today but also preserves resources for future generations. Therefore, all strategies, plans, programs, and development projects must integrate environmental protection and climate change adaptation requirements right from the policy-making stage, instead of dealing with the consequences after development. artigo.texto: Specialist investment firm Adaptogen Capital is targeting a €1 billion ($1.61 billion) investment opportunity across European battery energy storage system (BESS) markets by 2030. As part of the company’s approach, it is exploring capital raisings for 2027. The funds would help finance its initial European BESS assets, with an estimated requirement of €260 million in equity and €500 million in debt. The company has developed a 1.2-gigawatt pipeline of Belgian BESS opportunities, with five initial projects in development and progressing towards final investment decisions. Through its operating platform MVA Energy, Adaptogen Capital aims to address grid congestion and the integration of growing renewable generation, alongside a parallel German pipeline. Adaptogen has also progressed a further 500-megawatt (MW) portfolio across two sites in Germany, located at key offshore wind high-voltage landing points on the transmission grid. Adaptogen Capital Managing Director James Mills says grids across Europe are under growing pressure from the pace of renewable buildout, creating a clear investment case for well-located, grid-scale battery storage with firm connections, backed by structured revenue and debt facilities. “We have spent the past three years building a pipeline that targets that opportunity, and our approach of committing capital once projects have reached final investment decision allows infrastructure investors to back assets where development risks have already been substantially reduced,” Mills says. Going beyond the UK Adaptogen’s European ambitions build directly on its UK experience. The company’s original fund, which closed in 2023, has been fully committed to developing and operating BESS assets through Varco Energy, with a follow-on co-investment raised in 2025. Varco Energy’s operational projects include Native River — the UK’s longest-duration transmission-connected battery installation — and Sizing John Phase One. Native River, located south of Liverpool, has a system capacity of 57MW and 138MW hours. It delivers grid-balancing services such as frequency regulation, reserve capacity, and load shifting to support renewable energy integration. The phase-one Sizing John Project is located near St Helens and supports NESO in operating the Mersey Ring. The project is designed to allow for potential expansion as grid demand grows. Adaptogen Capital says that investor appetite for European battery energy storage is strengthening and growing grid constraints reinforce the role of storage as critical energy infrastructure. With few specialist BESS managers operating at scale across Europe, the company says its project-led approach is well aligned with the needs of infrastructure investors seeking exposure to a key asset class in the next phase of the energy transition. Write to Aaliyah Rogan at Mining.com.au Main image: Adaptogen Capital

artigo.texto: HDOT, Sustainability Partners and Hensel Phelps Mark the Start of Construction on Oʻahu and Kauaʻi Microgrids with PV, BESS and Charging Infrastructure The State of Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation (HDOT), Sustainability Partners (SP), and Hensel Phelps have marked the start of construction on new microgrid projects on Oʻahu and Kauaʻi that include solar PV canopies, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and electric vehicle charging stations. Construction Hawaiian Blessing ceremonies commemorating the start of construction were held in August. The projects are designed to strengthen energy resilience at critical HDOT facilities by integrating solar generation with battery energy storage and intelligent microgrid controls to manage energy generation, storage, and use. Together, the projects are expected to generate 2.2 MWh of renewable energy each day and will include two 1 MW battery energy storage systems. The microgrids are part of HDOT’s broader work to modernize HDOT’s infrastructure and advance the state’s clean energy and resilience goals. “These projects represent another important step in strengthening the resiliency of Hawaiʻi’s infrastructure,” said Ed Sniffen, Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation Director. “These PV and battery storage systems provide critical energy security for our teams during severe weather and multi-day blackouts.” Oʻahu The Oʻahu microgrid will serve HDOT Highways’ Oʻahu District Main Office Facility on Kakoi Street. The project includes a 1 MW battery energy storage system and solar PV canopies expected to generate 1.5 MWh of renewable energy per day. This site will include over 40 Level 2 Chargers and 1 Dual-Port 200 kW DC Fast Charger. Schneider Electric’s EcoStruxure microgrid technology will provide the intelligent control layer that coordinates solar generation, battery storage, EV charging, and interaction with the utility grid to optimize how energy is generated, stored, and used. SP is also working with Hawaiian Electric toward enrollment in its Energy Export program, which would allow the site to export surplus power back to the electric grid. Kauaʻi The Kauaʻi microgrid will serve HDOT Highways’ Kauaʻi District Main Office Facility on Haleukana Street. The project includes a 1 MW battery energy storage system and solar PV canopies expected to generate 700 kWh of renewable energy per day. This site will include over 12 Level 2 Chargers and 1 Dual-Port 200 kW DC Fast Charger. As on Oʻahu, Schneider Electric’s EcoStruxure microgrid technology will provide centralized visibility and intelligent control of the site’s distributed energy resources, helping coordinate generation, storage, and electrical loads. Hensel Phelps is leading construction of both projects and has worked alongside HDOT and Sustainability Partners on transportation and energy infrastructure throughout Hawaiʻi.
